## TL;DR
GLP-1 leads the named discoveries in my forecast at 22%, backed by established clinical benefits and sustained scientific recognition ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/)). Orexin ranks second at 12%, with new treatment validation strengthening its discovery-to-disease story ([FDA](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms)). Other is the largest single outcome at 29% because the list omits serious contenders, including DNA sensing and targeted leukemia therapy ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/); [Collège de France](https://www.college-de-france.fr/en/news/the-shaw-prize-in-biological-and-medical-sciences-awarded-to-professor-hugues-de-the)).

## Context
The Medicine prize is scheduled for Monday, 5 October 2026, at 11:30 CEST at the earliest, equivalent to 09:30 UTC. This forecast uses information available at the client's stated cutoff, before that announcement. The current nominations and evaluations are confidential, so external awards establish scientific standing—not membership of a verified Nobel shortlist ([official schedule](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates/); [Nobel selection process](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2025/04/annual-review-2024.pdf)).

I apply the client's discovery-based resolution rule. Different laureate names do not invalidate an option. For a divided prize, discovery shares—not individual laureate shares—determine the outcome, with announcement order breaking an equal-share tie. Attribution still matters to selection because a Nobel prize can recognize no more than three people ([Nobel statutes](https://www.nobelprize.org/statutes-of-the-nobel-foundation/)).

## Evidence
The historical backbone is a forward-looking precursor-award reference class. I checked every annual Lasker Basic Medical Research Award from 2010 through 2025 against that calendar year's Medicine Nobel. The unit is an awarded discovery, not a recipient. There were fifteen awarded discoveries because the 2020 awards were canceled; only one had a substantively corresponding same-year Medicine Nobel, a raw frequency of 7%. These are fixed historical award records examined at the forecast cutoff, not a calibrated probability for orexin ([Lasker archive](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/); [Nobel archive](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/)). The complete audit window follows.

| Award year | Lasker Basic discovery | Corresponding Medicine Nobel that year? |
|---|---|---|
| [2010](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2010/summary/) | [Leptin and body-weight regulation](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/leptin-a-hormone-that-regulates-appetite-and-body-weight/) | No |
| [2011](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2011/summary/) | [Chaperone-assisted protein folding](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/) | No |
| [2012](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2012/summary/) | [Motor proteins and cell movement](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/motor-proteins-that-contract-muscles-and-enable-cell-movements/) | No |
| [2013](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2013/summary/) | [Regulated neurotransmitter release](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/regulated-neurotransmitter-release/) | Yes, within the broader vesicle-traffic discovery |
| [2014](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2014/summary/) | [Unfolded protein response](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/) | No |
| [2015](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2015/summary/) | [DNA-damage response](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/discoveries-concerning-the-dna-damage-response/) | No |
| [2016](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2016/summary/) | [Oxygen sensing](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/oxygen-sensing-an-essential-process-for-survival/) | No |
| [2017](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2017/summary/) | [TOR and cell growth](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/nutrient-activated-tor-proteins-that-regulate-cell-growth/) | No |
| [2018](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2018/summary/) | [Histone modifications](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/histone-modifications-and-gene-expression/) | No |
| [2019](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2019/summary/) | [B- and T-cell lineages](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/b-and-t-cells-the-organizing-principle-of-the-adaptive-immune-system/) | No |
| 2020 | [Awards canceled](https://laskerfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/2020_awards_cancellation_press_release.pdf) | Excluded from denominator |
| [2021](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2021/summary/) | [Optogenetics](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/light-sensitive-microbial-proteins-optogenetics/) | No |
| [2022](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2022/summary/) | [Integrins and cell adhesion](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/integrins-mediators-of-cell-matrix-cell-adhesion/) | No |
| [2023](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2023/summary/) | [AlphaFold](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/alphafold-a-technology-for-predicting-protein-structures/) | No |
| [2024](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2024/summary/) | [cGAS-mediated DNA sensing](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/) | No |
| [2025](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2025/summary/) | [Low-complexity protein domains](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/2025-winners/) | No |

The sole overlap requires care. Südhof's neurotransmitter-release work formed part of the broader vesicle-traffic Nobel, whose other laureates had already received a Lasker for related work in 2002. It was not simply a newly recognized discovery advancing immediately to Stockholm ([2013 Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2013/summary/); [2002 Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/membrane-fusion-and-organelle-formation/)). This history limits a mechanical September-to-October award boost. It does not establish a penalty for receiving a Lasker in the same year.

GLP-1 has the strongest named combination of foundational physiology, demonstrated medical benefit, and sustained recognition. Its discovery and therapeutic development received the 2024 Lasker Clinical Award, followed by the 2025 Breakthrough Prize announced on 5 April 2025. Clarivate added recognition for identification and biological characterization on 17 September 2026 ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/); [Breakthrough](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/91); [Clarivate](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/)). Its medical case also extends beyond weight-loss publicity: the FDA approved semaglutide for reducing serious cardiovascular events in the specified overweight or obese population on 8 March 2024 ([FDA](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-treatment-reduce-risk-serious-heart-problems-specifically-adults-obesity-or)). I read this as a mature discovery-to-health transformation, not just a fashionable drug story.

Orexin has the strongest recent scientific update. The 2026 Lasker Basic Award recognized its role in maintaining wakefulness and causing narcolepsy when deficient. The discovery already had older validation through the 2023 Breakthrough Prize, announced in September 2022 ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/orexin-a-brain-peptide-that-maintains-wakefulness/); [Breakthrough](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/73)). On 5 August 2026, the FDA approved oveporexton, which directly restores deficient orexin signaling. The release reports two randomized, placebo-controlled, twelve-week studies involving 273 adults; it does not provide their calendar recruitment windows or a long postmarketing record ([FDA](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms)). That is a coherent mechanism-to-disease-to-treatment arc. I place it below GLP-1 because GLP-1's therapeutic impact is broader and longer established, not because orexin's recent Lasker makes it ineligible.

The remaining options retain substantial combined probability. The estimates below are my comparative judgments; the linked sources establish their scientific cases, not the numerical probabilities.

| Discovery | Rounded forecast | Main assessment |
|---|---:|---|
| CAR-T | 6% | Transformative cellular therapy. The June 2026 Tang citation strengthens its standing but includes TIL therapy, creating motivation-framing risk ([Tang Prize](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097)). |
| Unfolded protein response | 6% | A clear cellular stress-signaling discovery with a compact core attribution; no clinical breakthrough is required for its scientific case ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/)). |
| Optogenetics | 6% | A powerful method for causal neuroscience. I discount attribution complexity more than hypothetical Chemistry competition ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/light-sensitive-microbial-proteins-optogenetics/)). |
| Chaperone-assisted folding | 6% | A settled biological mechanism. Category uncertainty warrants a modest discount, but computational structure prediction is a different achievement ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/); [2024 Chemistry Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/)). |
| PCSK9 | 3% | Strong human-genetics-to-treatment logic. The FDA's 17 July 2026 oral-inhibitor announcement adds validation, but extends an already established target ([FDA](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-oral-pcsk9-inhibitor-lower-ldl-cholesterol-adults-high-cholesterol)). |
| Inherited breast/ovarian cancer susceptibility | 2% | Major diagnostic and preventive impact; mapping, gene identification, and broader susceptibility research complicate the award's boundaries ([NCI](https://www.cancer.gov/research/progress/discovery/brca)). |
| Next-generation sequencing | 2% | Enormous biomedical importance, with a substantial discount for this specific prize category rather than scientific quality ([Princess of Asturias](https://www.fpa.es/en/princess-of-asturias-awards/laureates/2026-david-klenerman-shankar-balasubramanian-pascal-mayer/); [Nobel category history](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/themes/the-nobel-prize-in-physiology-or-medicine-1901-2000/)). |
| Wnt and organoids | 2% | Strong developmental and stem-cell biology, but a less predictable combined discovery-and-application framing ([Gairdner](https://www.gairdner.org/winner/roel-nusse)). |
| Anti-TNF | 2% | A mature therapeutic paradigm with clear central attribution. A long wait neither makes it due nor proves rejection ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/anti-tnf-for-treating-rheumatoid-arthritis/)). |
| Leptin | 2% | Foundational body-weight physiology; GLP-1 currently has the stronger combined physiology-and-treatment case ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/leptin-a-hormone-that-regulates-appetite-and-body-weight/)). |

Other is an affirmative assessment of omitted competition, not merely a reserve for surprise. It includes TOR-mediated growth regulation and cGAS-mediated DNA sensing, both supported by major basic-research awards ([TOR](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/nutrient-activated-tor-proteins-that-regulate-cell-growth/); [cGAS](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/)). Current recognition also supports optical coherence tomography, acute promyelocytic leukemia mechanisms and targeted treatment, fetal-to-adult hemoglobin switching, and inherited-retinal-disease gene therapy ([Clarivate, September 2026](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/); [Shaw recognition, May 2026](https://www.college-de-france.fr/en/news/the-shaw-prize-in-biological-and-medical-sciences-awarded-to-professor-hugues-de-the); [Breakthrough, April 2026](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/98)). Their breadth supports keeping Other above every individual discovery.

Numerically, I pooled the candidate assessments, gave greatest weight to scientific importance and maturity, and made bounded adjustments for verified new evidence, attribution, and category fit. I increased GLP-1's relative weight, retained orexin's clinical-validation uplift without an automatic same-year-Lasker premium, and reduced excessive category discounts on UPR and optogenetics. I preserved a separate omitted-discovery allocation, then normalized the listed weights. This is structured judgment, not a fitted model of committee behavior. No prediction-market prices, betting odds, or public probability aggregates informed the calculation.

## What's non-obvious
**September recognition is not a new nomination opportunity.** The Nobel timetable places the nomination deadline in January, external assessment through the following months, and committee recommendations in September. Recent Lasker and Clarivate selections therefore validate science already available for consideration; they do not show that a new candidate entered the Nobel process at the last minute ([Nobel selection timetable](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2025/04/annual-review-2024.pdf)). I also treat multiple awards for the same discovery as partly correlated judgments, not independent votes whose effects should be multiplied.

Discovery-based resolution removes much of the apparent roster risk. Habener's death on 28 December 2025 changes the possible GLP-1 laureate allocation, but does not remove the discovery from contention; Clarivate's current Drucker–Holst–Mojsov grouping supplies a different compact formulation ([ASBMB memorial, March 2026](https://www.asbmb.org/asbmb-today/people/031626/in-memoriam-joel-habener); [Clarivate](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/)). Conversely, matching names alone is insufficient: a cellular-immunotherapy prize centered on TIL rather than CAR-T could resolve Other despite recognizing people listed in the CAR-T option ([Tang citation](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097)).

## Uncertainties
The largest missing evidence is the confidential candidate evaluation, not another clinical headline. A credible contemporaneous shortlist, the committee's preferred discovery framing, and its comparative assessments would materially sharpen this forecast. Those records are unavailable under the Nobel confidentiality rules ([Nobel statutes](https://www.nobelprize.org/statutes-of-the-nobel-foundation/)). The precursor reference class also contains only one positive observation, and archived award pages do not consistently preserve exact original announcement dates. I use it to discipline timing claims, not to estimate candidate-specific odds.

Category assignment and broad motivations remain consequential. Protein-folding mechanisms are not the same discovery as computational structure prediction, and UPR is distinct from chaperone-assisted folding ([Lasker folding citation](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/); [UPR citation](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/); [Chemistry Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/)). I impose neither a mandatory field-rotation rule nor an overdue-discovery rule. The diffuse distribution reflects these unresolved choices. The six decimal places preserve normalization arithmetic; they do not imply millionth-level knowledge of the committee's decision.
sub_write_ups:
## Forecast as of 1 October 2026, 20:55 UTC

The prize is scheduled to be announced on Monday, 5 October 2026 at 11:30 CEST at the earliest. The Nobel process remains unusually opaque: nominations were due by 31 January, evaluation runs from February into early October, and current nominations and deliberations are confidential. I found no credible leak or committee-linked information. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates?sm_guid=Mjk3MzM1fDI0MDExMjE4fC0xfHJzaGFsZXR0QHJlc2VhcmNoYW1lcmljYS5vcmd8MjM3MTYzMXx8MHwwfDMwMjE2OTQ3NXw5NTN8MHwwfHwyNjI2NDR8MA2&utm_source=openai))

My leading forecast is **GLP-1 at 18.0%**, narrowly ahead of **orexin at 17.0%**. I assign **32.5% to Other**, reflecting both the inherent difficulty of predicting an exact Nobel discovery and several strong omitted candidates. The top two are close enough that they should be viewed as essentially co-favorites rather than as a decisive ranking.

## Method

I did not use prediction-market prices, betting odds, or public forecast aggregates. I combined three approaches:

1. **Structural Nobel-worthiness:** magnitude and maturity of the discovery, whether its full medical importance is established, and whether it can be expressed as a clear Nobel motivation.
2. **Laureate feasibility:** whether historical credit can plausibly be allocated to no more than three living people. Because resolution is by discovery rather than exact laureate names, roster mismatches do not invalidate an option, but they can make the Nobel committee less likely to select the discovery.
3. **Timing and weak signals:** major precursor prizes, their distance from 2026, new regulatory or clinical validation, current scientific-award clustering, category competition with Chemistry, and proximity to recently awarded Nobel subjects.

For the named candidates I weighted scientific impact and maturity most heavily, followed by attribution clarity and precursor-prize timing. Topic rotation, category fit, age or mortality urgency, and 2026 weak signals received smaller weights. I then reserved a separate probability for omitted discoveries rather than forcing the listed candidates to exhaust nearly all probability.

As a timing check, I hand-matched 13 major precursor-award events to nine recent Medicine Nobel outcomes. The lag distribution was: 0 of 13 in the same year, 5 of 13 after one to three years, 5 of 13 after four to ten years, and 3 of 13 after more than ten years; median lag was four years. This is a positively selected sample of successes, not a conversion rate, but it cautions against treating a September 2026 award as a direct Nobel signal. It favors candidates with both fresh recognition and an older precursor, such as GLP-1, orexin, CAR-T, sequencing and optogenetics.

## Most important weak signals

### 1. Orexin: the strongest genuinely new signal

On 5 August 2026 the FDA approved oveporexton, the first medicine that directly restores the orexin signaling lost in narcolepsy type 1 and treats the disorder's underlying biology rather than only individual symptoms. The approval was based on two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 12-week trials enrolling 273 adults. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms?utm_source=openai))

In September, Emmanuel Mignot and Masashi Yanagisawa received the 2026 Lasker Basic Medical Research Award for identifying orexin and showing that orexin deficiency causes narcolepsy. The Lasker account explicitly links the discovery to the newly approved orexin agonist. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/2026-winners/?utm_source=openai))

This is an unusually coherent discovery-to-disease-to-causal-therapy arc, and Mignot and Yanagisawa had already received the 2023 Breakthrough Prize. The negative is that the history also includes Luis de Lecea, Takeshi Sakurai, Greg Sutcliffe and others, so attribution is less perfectly clean than the two-person Lasker citation implies. Same-year Lasker-to-Nobel transitions also appear uncommon. These considerations keep orexin at 17%, rather than allowing the striking August–September sequence to dominate the forecast.

### 2. GLP-1: strongest mature and socially consequential case

The 2024 Lasker Clinical Award recognized Joel Habener, Svetlana Mojsov and Lotte Bjerre Knudsen for the discovery and development of GLP-1-based obesity drugs. Its account connects identification of the active hormone to the development of liraglutide and semaglutide and describes the resulting transformation of diabetes and obesity treatment. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/))

On 17 September 2026, Clarivate named Daniel Drucker, Jens Juul Holst and Svetlana Mojsov as Citation Laureates for identifying and characterizing GLP-1 and its biological activity. That is a Nobel-compatible three-person formulation and a modest positive signal, though Citation Laureates identify Nobel-class work rather than predicting a particular award year. ([clarivate.com](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/?utm_source=openai))

The main negative is unusually contested credit. Major prizes have variously recognized Habener, Mojsov, Knudsen, Holst and Drucker, while other contributors include John Eng and Richard DiMarchi. Habener died on 28 December 2025, eliminating one central pioneer from Nobel eligibility. ([hopkinsmedicine.org](https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/news/articles/2026/04/a-titan-in-endocrinology)) This attribution problem likely explains some of the delay and prevents me from assigning the discovery a much higher probability. Nevertheless, GLP-1 has a favorable two-year lag from its Lasker, immense established medical impact, and a field—metabolic physiology—not recently represented in the Medicine Nobel. I therefore place it narrowly first at 18%.

### 3. CAR-T: major 2026 award configuration, but a topic-rotation problem

The June 2026 Tang Prize selected Steven Rosenberg, Michel Sadelain and Carl June for cellular immunotherapy encompassing tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and CAR-T therapy. It provides a prominent three-person configuration close to the option's named researchers. ([tang-prize.org](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097&utm_source=openai))

CAR-T has generated durable remissions and established engineered cells as living medicines. Against that, the Tang citation is broader than CAR-T alone, foundational CAR inventor Zelig Eshhar died in 2025, and the 2025 Medicine Nobel recognized peripheral immune tolerance immediately after earlier immunology and cancer-immunotherapy prizes. Those headwinds reduce CAR-T to 5.8% despite its strong recent award momentum.

### 4. Important omitted contenders support a large Other probability

Other is not merely generic uncertainty. It includes several credible, specifically identified rivals:

- **Optical coherence tomography:** Clarivate's 2026 medicine selections included James Fujimoto, David Huang and Eric Swanson, a clean trio previously recognized by the 2023 Lasker Clinical Award. ([clarivate.com](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/?utm_source=openai))
- **Acute promyelocytic leukemia:** the 2026 Shaw Prize recognized Anne Déjean, Hugues de Thé and Zhu Chen for the molecular basis of APL and a synergistic targeted therapy that transformed it into one of the most curable cancers. ([college-de-france.fr](https://www.college-de-france.fr/en/news/the-shaw-prize-in-biological-and-medical-sciences-awarded-to-professor-hugues-de-the))
- **B- and T-lymphocyte discovery:** Max Cooper and Jacques Miller remain frequently cited, very elderly candidates with a classic fundamental-immunology case.
- **cGAS–STING signaling, immune-cell adhesion receptors, mTOR, base editing and other gene-editing methods:** each is plausible enough to consume nontrivial probability even though no single one dominates the residual.

Because these are real alternatives rather than remote possibilities, I reserve 32.5% for Other.

## Assessment of every listed option

| Option | Probability | Main considerations |
|---|---:|---|
| GLP-1 | 18.0% | Largest demonstrated population impact; favorable 2024–26 prize sequence; metabolism is due. Reduced by a five-plus-person credit dispute and Habener's death. |
| Orexin | 17.0% | Strongest new 2026 convergence: causal FDA-approved therapy plus Lasker recognition and a 2023 Breakthrough Prize. Reduced by same-year Lasker timing and multiple discovery contributors. |
| CAR-T | 5.8% | Transformative living-drug platform and exact 2026 Tang trio. Reduced by 2025 immune-tolerance Nobel, the broader TIL/CAR-T framing and the death of Eshhar. |
| Next-generation sequencing | 4.9% | One of the most consequential technologies in modern biology; multiple 2022–26 awards. Pascal Mayer is a likely third laureate, and a 2026 Zurich award explicitly classified the work as chemistry, creating substantial category leakage. ([news.uzh.ch](https://news.uzh.ch/en/articles/news/2026/gretener-thuerlemann-prize.html)) |
| Optogenetics | 4.6% | Revolutionized experimental neuroscience and sits at a plausible five-year lag from its 2021 Lasker. Lowered by disagreement over whether Deisseroth, Hegemann, Miesenböck, Boyden, Nagel or the late Dieter Oesterhelt deserves the three slots.  |
| Unfolded protein response | 3.9% | Exceptionally clean Mori–Walter pairing, fundamental mechanism and extensive precursor recognition. The absence of a distinctive 2026 trigger and overlap with broader proteostasis research are the main negatives.  |
| Chaperone-mediated protein folding | 3.4% | Clear Horwich–Hartl collaboration with major Lasker, Shaw and Breakthrough recognition. It competes with Chemistry and is conceptually adjacent to the 1972 protein-folding Nobel.  |
| Inherited breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility | 2.8% | Enormous impact on cancer prevention and precision treatment, with an intuitively Nobel-worthy King–Skolnick–Stratton configuration. Credit is divided among linkage, BRCA1 cloning and BRCA2 discovery, making the motivation less unitary.  |
| PCSK9 | 2.4% | Elegant human-genetics-to-drug story. The July 2026 approval of the first oral PCSK9 inhibitor adds a genuine translational milestone. It is discounted because cholesterol regulation already received the 1985 Medicine Nobel and precursor-prize consensus on the exact trio is weaker.  |
| Leptin | 1.8% | Foundational demonstration that body weight is hormonally regulated and newly salient in the obesity era. Douglas Coleman, Friedman's canonical co-discoverer, is deceased, while O'Rahilly's work is more accurately characterized as human obesity genetics.  |
| TNF therapy | 1.7% | One of the great bench-to-bedside successes in autoimmune medicine, with a very clean Feldmann–Maini pair and substantial age urgency. Penalized heavily because it would follow the 2025 immune-tolerance prize and because its major Lasker recognition dates to 2003.  |
| Wnt signaling and organoids | 1.2% | Both achievements are Nobel caliber, but the option bundles Nusse's Wnt discovery with Clevers's later organoid platform. They are related yet distinct discoveries with different contributor sets, making a single official motivation awkward.  |

## Calibration and uncertainty

The probabilities are deliberately diffuse. Nobel forecasting differs from ordinary award forecasting because there is no public shortlist, the final outcome can come from dozens of mature fields, and public scientific prizes are signals of worthiness rather than reliable signals of the exact year. The roughly three-and-a-half-day horizon does not substantially reduce that uncertainty because the Nobel Assembly's information remains private.

My largest judgment call is the balance between GLP-1 and orexin. A model emphasizing typical precursor-prize lag and broad medical impact favors GLP-1. A weak-signal model emphasizing the August 2026 causal therapy and September 2026 Lasker favors orexin. I combine those views rather than selecting one aggressively. The final probabilities sum exactly to 1.0.

## Forecast summary and cutoff

**My leading individual discovery is GLP-1, at 23.400%; however, the combined “Other” category is slightly more likely, at 24.750%.** Optogenetics is the next-highest listed discovery, at 10.400%. This is a relatively diffuse forecast: I do not find evidence sufficient to make any discovery an overwhelming favorite.

The information cutoff is **October 1, 2026, at 20:55 UTC**. NobelPrize.org schedules the announcement for **October 5, 2026, at 11:30 CEST at the earliest**, equivalent to 09:30 UTC—84 hours and 35 minutes after the cutoff. I exclude subsequent information. The nomination and evaluation process is confidential for 50 years, so public prize citations and scientific accomplishments are indirect evidence, not a known Nobel shortlist. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates/?sm_guid=Mjk3MzM1fDI0MDExMjE4fC0xfHJzaGFsZXR0QHJlc2VhcmNoYW1lcmljYS5vcmd8MjM3MTYzMXx8MHwwfDI3NzgwMzExOHw5NTN8MHwwfHwyNjI2NDR8MA2&utm_source=openai))

I apply the question’s discovery-based resolution rule. A GLP-1 award remains a GLP-1 outcome even if the laureates include Joel Habener or Daniel Drucker rather than exactly the three people listed. Likewise, a sequencing award including Pascal Mayer would still match next-generation sequencing. Attribution difficulty can affect the committee’s willingness to select a discovery, but a mismatch in names is **not** itself a reason to allocate probability to Other.

## 1. Research approach and decision-relevant questions

I used official Nobel historical records, the Nobel data API, primary award citations from Lasker and Breakthrough, FDA announcements, and institutional sources. Two independent research briefs examined omitted discoveries and the therapeutic candidates. A separate historical audit checked Nobel–Lasker overlaps. I also searched English and Swedish material and checked a news API, but did not use unsourced publicity, chatbot predictions, or article counts as quantitative signals.

The main research questions were:

1. **Does GLP-1 have more than a fashionable obesity-drug narrative?** Its foundational history, major-prize convergence, and demonstrated medical applications support a strong case.
2. **Has orexin acquired genuinely new evidence of Nobel readiness in 2026?** Yes: both a Lasker award and an FDA-reported approval targeting deficient orexin signaling. This increased my allocation.
3. **Are there enough strong omitted discoveries to justify substantial Other probability?** Yes, especially cGAS/STING, non-invasive prenatal testing, gene therapy, fetal-hemoglobin regulation, mTOR, and cellular organization.
4. **How predictive is a September precursor award for an October Nobel?** The historical audit cautions against treating a current-year Lasker as a near-certain imminent Nobel.
5. **Which candidates might be recognized in Chemistry instead of Medicine?** This is particularly important for sequencing and, to a lesser extent, protein-folding research.

No prediction-market prices, betting odds, or numerical public forecast aggregates were consulted. The final probabilities are my own judgmental estimates, informed by the evidence below.

## 5. Numerical construction and reproducibility

I constructed three complete, mutually exclusive probability profiles. These are **judgmental models, not statistically fitted likelihoods**:

- **A, clinical-impact emphasis, weight 45%:** favors discoveries with highly visible demonstrated medical benefits, particularly GLP-1.
- **B, mature fundamental-biology emphasis, weight 40%:** gives more weight to longstanding cellular and physiological discoveries.
- **C, tools-and-surprise emphasis, weight 15%:** raises research technologies and retains more probability for omitted discoveries.

These weights reflect my assessment of the current candidate set, not an alleged historical frequency of committee preferences. All three profiles incorporate the research above. Each column sums to 100%.

| Outcome | A: clinical impact | B: fundamental biology | C: tools/surprise | Final |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GLP-1 | 34.0% | 15.0% | 14.0% | 23.400% |
| Optogenetics | 8.0% | 11.0% | 16.0% | 10.400% |
| CAR-T | 10.0% | 4.0% | 3.5% | 6.625% |
| Unfolded protein response | 3.5% | 9.5% | 6.5% | 6.350% |
| PCSK9 | 3.5% | 2.0% | 2.0% | 2.675% |
| Next-generation sequencing | 2.5% | 3.0% | 7.0% | 3.375% |
| Orexin | 7.0% | 6.5% | 6.5% | 6.725% |
| Wnt/organoids | 2.5% | 3.5% | 3.0% | 2.975% |
| Leptin | 1.5% | 2.5% | 1.5% | 1.900% |
| Anti-TNF | 1.5% | 1.0% | 1.0% | 1.225% |
| Chaperone-mediated folding | 4.0% | 11.0% | 6.0% | 7.100% |
| Inherited cancer susceptibility | 2.5% | 2.5% | 2.5% | 2.500% |
| Other | 19.5% | 28.5% | 30.5% | 24.750% |

For each outcome i, I calculated in Python:

**p(i) = 0.45 × A(i) + 0.40 × B(i) + 0.15 × C(i).**

For example, GLP-1 is 0.45 × 0.34 + 0.40 × 0.15 + 0.15 × 0.14 = **0.23400**. Other is 0.45 × 0.195 + 0.40 × 0.285 + 0.15 × 0.305 = **0.24750**. Python verified that each profile and the final distribution sum to 1.0.

The additional decimal places preserve the arithmetic of the ensemble; they do **not** imply that committee behavior can be estimated to five-decimal-place accuracy. The uncertain inputs are scientific framing, attribution, category choice, and undisclosed committee preferences. A 10-percentage-point transfer of model weight from B to A, for example, raises GLP-1 by 1.9 percentage points. Orexin could also exceed my central estimate materially if the committee places exceptional weight on its newly completed therapeutic narrative.

Finally, the short time to announcement does not itself justify high confidence. There is little remaining time for new scientific evidence, but the principal unknown is the confidential selection. My final allocation therefore keeps approximately three-quarters of the probability outside GLP-1 and approximately one-quarter outside all twelve named discoveries.

## 1. Resolution interpretation and institutional uncertainty

I forecast the **discovery named in the official motivation**, not the exact laureate slate. Thus, a GLP-1 prize naming Drucker rather than Knudsen would still match the GLP-1 option. Similarly, alternative contributors to optogenetics, sequencing, or CAR-T would not automatically push those outcomes into Other. Attribution difficulty matters only insofar as it might make the committee defer a discovery or choose a different scientific framing.

For a split prize, shares must be aggregated **by discovery**, rather than comparing individual laureates' shares. I apply the client's larger-discovery-share rule and, for equal discovery shares, the first-mentioned-discovery rule. A broad cellular-immunotherapy award could require particular care: CAR-T would match the listed option, but a motivation centered on tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes rather than CAR-T might resolve Other.

There is no verified public shortlist on which to condition. Nobel nominations are confidential for 50 years, and the prize can recognize at most three people. These constraints make external awards useful indicators of scientific stature, but not evidence that a particular discovery is on this year's final ballot. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/facts-on-the-nobel-prize-in-physiology-or-medicine/?utm_source=openai))

I prioritized official Nobel records, first-party scientific-award citations, FDA announcements, and primary clinical research. This classification is subjective and overlapping; it is not a fitted estimate that a clinical discovery has a 30% chance in 2026. The coverage window is the announcements from **October 2, 2006, through October 6, 2025**, with **N = 20 prize years**, using the completed historical award record available at the forecast cutoff. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/laureates/?utm_source=openai))

## 3. Decision-relevant research threads

### A. Is GLP-1's case a mature discovery-to-health transformation, rather than predominantly current publicity?

**Yes.** The 2024 Lasker Clinical award recognized Habener, Mojsov, and Knudsen for the discovery and development of GLP-1-based obesity treatments. Its scientific account traces the work from hormone biology in the 1980s through physiological characterization and long-acting drug development. The **2025**, not 2026, Breakthrough Prize recognized five contributors: Drucker, Habener, Holst, Knudsen, and Mojsov. These awards establish a mature scientific and translational case, although their differing recipient sets illustrate attribution complexity. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/))

The clinical evidence extends beyond weight loss. SELECT randomized **17,604 participants** with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity, but without diabetes. The trial ran from **October 24, 2018, through June 29, 2023**; the sponsor's report specifies a database cutoff of **July 18, 2023**. The primary publication appeared on **November 11, 2023**, and was updated on November 30. At a **mean follow-up of 39.8 months**, cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke occurred in **6.5% versus 8.0%**, with a hazard ratio of **0.80**. These are cumulative trial outcomes—not annual event rates—and the hazard ratio should not be confused with the ratio of the rounded percentages. This evidence substantially strengthens the Nobel-readiness argument. ([novonordisk-trials.com](https://www.novonordisk-trials.com/content/dam/nntrials/global/en/studies/data/4388-ctr-synopsis-nntrials-redacted.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Two 2026 developments add support. On **September 17, 2026**, Clarivate recognized Drucker, Holst, and Mojsov for GLP-1 identification, characterization, and biological activity. On **January 13, 2026**, FDA requested removal of suicidal-ideation/behavior warning language after its comprehensive review found no increased risk. The latter reduces one possible concern; it does not establish that these medicines have no other adverse effects. ([clarivate.com](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/?utm_source=openai))

I also investigated an eligibility issue raised during research. ASBMB's **March 16, 2026** memorial confirms that Habener died on **December 28, 2025**. This changes the potential laureate allocation, but does not eliminate the GLP-1 discovery from consideration. I treat the net effect as modest: several alternative allocations remain plausible, and the question does not require Habener—or any exact trio—to win. ([asbmb.org](https://www.asbmb.org/asbmb-today/people/031626/in-memoriam-joel-habener))

**Assessment:** GLP-1 has the strongest named combination of established biology, demonstrated medical benefit, and recognition across institutions. Its weaknesses are a crowded attribution history and uncertainty about whether the committee prioritizes it this year. It is a leading candidate, not an overwhelming favorite.

### B. Has orexin acquired a particularly strong 2026 mechanism-to-treatment package?

**Yes, and this was the largest discovery-specific upward update.** The Lasker Foundation's current award citation explicitly identifies its **2026 Basic Medical Research Award** with Mignot and Yanagisawa. The underlying discoveries span peptide identification in 1998, animal narcolepsy causality in 1999, and human orexin-deficiency evidence in 2000. The citation also describes de Lecea's contribution, so a Nobel recipient set differing from the Lasker pair would still fit the listed discovery. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/orexin-a-brain-peptide-that-maintains-wakefulness/))

FDA approved **Orzeyful/oveporexton on August 5, 2026**, directly targeting deficient orexin signaling in adult narcolepsy type 1. Its announcement reports two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled **12-week studies involving 273 adults**. The release supplies the evaluation duration but not the trials' calendar recruitment windows; I therefore do not treat this as evidence of a long postmarketing record. FDA also distinguished approval from lawful marketing following DEA scheduling. I verified the approval, but did not independently establish completion of that additional scheduling step by the cutoff. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms))

This gives orexin an unusually coherent package: fundamental physiology, a causal disease mechanism, a compact potential laureate allocation, and direct therapeutic validation. Its disadvantages relative to GLP-1 are the narrower clinical reach and much newer agonist-treatment record. I count the award and drug approval as a **joint, partly correlated signal**, not as two independent pieces of evidence whose probabilities can simply be multiplied.

### C. Do recent developments materially strengthen CAR-T and PCSK9?

**Yes, moderately.** CAR-T already had substantial scientific recognition: the 2024 Gairdner award honored Eshhar and Sadelain for CD19 CAR-T conception, development, and application. On **June 16, 2026**, the Tang Prize selected Rosenberg, Sadelain, and June for TIL and CAR-T therapies. That supplies a recent, three-person recognition package, although its combined TIL/CAR-T framing is broader than the option being forecast. ([gairdner.org](https://www.gairdner.org/resource-hub/2024-canada-gairdner-award-winners-announced))

FDA's **June 27, 2025** removal of REMS requirements for established autologous CAR-T products supports clinical maturity and improved access. It did not remove important safety concerns or the requirement for long-term surveillance. I give CAR-T meaningful probability because of its transformative cancer-treatment record, while retaining discounts for attribution and motivation-framing uncertainty. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-eliminates-risk-evaluation-and-mitigation-strategies-rems-autologous-chimeric-antigen-receptor))

For PCSK9, I verified FDA's **July 17, 2026** approval of **Lipfendra/enlicitide**, the first oral PCSK9 inhibitor. This extends the established discovery-to-therapy story. However, the approval evidence concerned LDL-cholesterol reduction, not a new cardiovascular-outcomes trial of the oral drug itself. It strengthens the candidate without making it as compelling as GLP-1's broader package. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-oral-pcsk9-inhibitor-lower-ldl-cholesterol-adults-high-cholesterol))

After verifying these developments, I increased the relative evidence multiplier for CAR-T from 1.20 to 1.40 and PCSK9 from 1.10 to 1.40. A smaller GLP-1 adjustment moved its multiplier from 1.45 to 1.50. Together, these changes moved the initial independent estimates from approximately **6.88% to 7.83% for CAR-T** and **2.70% to 3.35% for PCSK9**. Orexin's probability decreased slightly through normalization, not because its scientific evidence weakened.

### D. Does the named list adequately cover the plausible winning discoveries?

**It covers many major candidates, but not sufficiently to make Other a small residual.** Important omissions include TOR/nutrient sensing, recognized by the 2017 Lasker Basic award; cGAS-mediated DNA sensing, recognized in 2024; and low-complexity-domain biology and cellular organization, recognized in 2025. These provide credible alternatives within foundational biology. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/nutrient-activated-tor-proteins-that-regulate-cell-growth/))

There are also strong omitted translational stories. The 2025 Lasker Clinical award recognized triple-drug cystic-fibrosis therapy. The **April 18, 2026** Breakthrough awards recognized inherited-retinal-disease gene therapy and the fetal-to-adult hemoglobin switch as a therapeutic target, among other work. Clarivate's 2026 Medicine recognitions also included optical coherence tomography and immune-system adhesion receptors. These recognitions do not establish near-term Nobel probabilities, but they demonstrate that a forecast confined too tightly to the twelve named discoveries would omit substantial competition. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/combined-triple-drug-therapy-for-cystic-fibrosis/))

## 4. Assessment of the remaining named discoveries

- **Chaperone-assisted folding:** A strong, settled, foundational cell-biology discovery with the 2011 Lasker Basic award. I retain substantial probability even without a major new 2026 catalyst. It ranks slightly above UPR in my structural starting weights, but that difference is uncertain. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/))
- **Unfolded protein response:** The 2014 Lasker Basic award establishes a clear, important intracellular quality-control discovery. Its potential laureate allocation is relatively compact. The lack of a conspicuous new clinical milestone is not disqualifying for a physiology prize. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/))
- **Optogenetics:** The 2021 Lasker Basic award supports its transformative role in causal neuroscience. I give it a meaningful chance, tempered by the breadth of the enabling-method history and competing neuroscience discoveries. The option's precise names do not determine resolution. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/light-sensitive-microbial-proteins-optogenetics/))
- **Next-generation sequencing:** The 2024 Gairdner recognition establishes a powerful biomedical-method case. My lower Medicine probability partly reflects category uncertainty: the 1980 sequencing Nobel was in Chemistry. That precedent is informative, not a rule preventing a Medicine award. ([gairdner.org](https://www.gairdner.org/resource-hub/2024-canada-gairdner-award-winners-announced))
- **Wnt/organoids:** Nusse's Gairdner citation documents the pathway's importance in development, cancer, stem cells, and organoid cultivation. I view this as a credible contender, but assign it less weight than the clearest mature discovery/recognition packages. ([gairdner.org](https://www.gairdner.org/winner/roel-nusse))
- **Inherited breast/ovarian cancer susceptibility:** King's 2014 Lasker recognition supports the discovery's importance. The allocation across genetic linkage, BRCA gene identification, and broader hereditary-cancer work is less straightforward, but the discovery remains eligible under the question's broad matching rule. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/2014-lasker-awards-winners/))
- **Leptin:** The 2010 Lasker Basic award supports a fundamental body-weight-regulation discovery. My lower probability reflects competition from GLP-1's stronger contemporary therapeutic arc, not a belief that leptin lacks Nobel-level significance. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/leptin-a-hormone-that-regulates-appetite-and-body-weight/))
- **Anti-TNF:** The 2003 Lasker Clinical award establishes a major therapeutic paradigm shift. I retain a positive probability, but do not assume that its long wait makes a 2026 award increasingly inevitable. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/anti-tnf-for-treating-rheumatoid-arthritis/))

## 5. Reproducible probability calculation

Because the committee's shortlist and deliberations are unavailable, a reliably fitted candidate-level model is not possible. I use an explicit **judgmental weighted-evidence model**. Its inputs should be understood as comparative assessments, not empirically estimated likelihood ratios.

First, I assign structural starting weights based principally on established scientific importance, maturity, previous recognition, category fit, and the omitted candidate pool. These weights sum to 1. They are a modeling baseline constructed for this forecast—not a claimed archived forecast made at the end of 2025.

Second, I apply bounded relative multipliers for the additional evidence discussed above. Leaving a multiplier at 1.00 means no extra uplift relative to the structural baseline; it does not mean that discovery has no supporting evidence.

| Discovery | Structural weight b | Evidence multiplier m | Unnormalized weight b × m |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GLP-1 | 0.180 | 1.50 | 0.27000 |
| Optogenetics | 0.070 | 1.00 | 0.07000 |
| CAR-T | 0.070 | 1.40 | 0.09800 |
| UPR | 0.080 | 1.00 | 0.08000 |
| PCSK9 | 0.030 | 1.40 | 0.04200 |
| Next-generation sequencing | 0.030 | 1.00 | 0.03000 |
| Orexin | 0.060 | 2.80 | 0.16800 |
| Wnt/organoids | 0.030 | 1.00 | 0.03000 |
| Leptin | 0.020 | 1.00 | 0.02000 |
| Anti-TNF | 0.020 | 1.00 | 0.02000 |
| Chaperone folding | 0.090 | 1.00 | 0.09000 |
| BRCA susceptibility genes | 0.035 | 1.00 | 0.03500 |
| Other | 0.285 | 1.05 | 0.29925 |

The normalization constant is **Z = 1.25225**, and each probability is calculated as **p(i) = b(i) × m(i) / Z**. For example, GLP-1 is 0.27000 / 1.25225 = 0.2156118986; orexin is 0.16800 / 1.25225 = 0.1341585147. I calculated the full vector in Python, rounded to six decimal places, and assigned Other the rounding residual so the reported probabilities sum exactly to 1.000000.

The baseline gives GLP-1 the highest named weight because its established case is already unusually strong. Chaperone folding and UPR receive substantial weights to preserve the historical plausibility of foundational biology. Orexin receives the largest multiplier because its verified 2026 developments most materially improve its annual award case. Other starts large because it represents numerous competing discoveries rather than one weak candidate.

## 6. Sensitivity and limits

I tested sensitivity to how strongly the 2026 signals should be interpreted, keeping the structural baseline unchanged:

- **Weaker signals:** multipliers of 1.15 for GLP-1, 1.80 for orexin, 1.15 for CAR-T, 1.15 for PCSK9, and 1.10 for Other; all remaining multipliers stay at 1.00. This produces approximately **18.51% GLP-1, 9.66% orexin, and 28.03% Other**.
- **Stronger signals:** corresponding multipliers of 1.80, 3.80, 1.55, 1.55, and 0.95. This produces approximately **23.95% GLP-1, 16.85% orexin, and 20.01% Other**.

These are reproducible scenario checks, **not confidence intervals**. Changing the structural judgments—especially the committee's relative appetite for fundamental biology versus clinical transformation—could produce wider variation. The largest remaining unknown is not whether these discoveries are important; it is which one the committee has evaluated most favorably for this particular year.

**Bottom line:** GLP-1 is the strongest named candidate, orexin has the strongest recent upward momentum, and a substantial Other allocation is necessary. None warrants anything close to a majority probability.

## Forecast summary

**Other is the most likely individual outcome, at 33.00%. GLP-1 is the strongest named discovery, at 19.56%, followed by orexin at 9.60% and chaperone-mediated protein folding at 8.15%.** This is a forecast of the discovery that will determine resolution—not of the exact laureate lineup.

The information cutoff is **October 1, 2026, at 20:55 UTC**. The official schedule places the Medicine announcement on **October 5, 2026, at 11:30 CEST at the earliest**, equivalent to 09:30 UTC. That is at least 84 hours and 35 minutes after the cutoff. I have not used a subsequent announcement or outcome. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates/?trk=test&utm_source=openai))

## 1. Interpretation and research method

I followed the client's discovery-based matching rule. In particular, GLP-1 can resolve YES even if the laureates include Joel Habener or Daniel Drucker rather than exactly the three people in the option. Similarly, inclusion of Pascal Mayer would not prevent next-generation sequencing from matching. Conversely, a scientist's name alone does not establish a match: an award to Steven Rosenberg for tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy would not automatically be a CAR-T award.

The main evidence sources were official Nobel records, the Lasker Foundation's award archives, Gairdner and Breakthrough Prize announcements, FDA announcements, and other award institutions. I also used the Nobel-data API, a historical-award audit, a specialist screen of unlisted candidates, and date-filtered news searches. News searches—including Swedish-language searches—were used to discover leads that could be checked against primary sources. **I did not use prediction-market prices, betting odds, or crowd probabilities.**

My decision-relevant research threads were:

1. **Has orexin recently acquired stronger clinical and award validation?** Yes: the 2026 Lasker Basic award and an August 2026 FDA approval substantially strengthen this listed candidate.
2. **Does the supplied shortlist omit serious, Medicine-native contenders?** Yes: APL therapy, BCL11A/hemoglobin switching, Notch, CFTR therapy, cGAS, and other discoveries warrant substantial Other probability.
3. **Which discoveries face meaningful competition from Chemistry?** I discounted sequencing particularly strongly, and applied smaller discounts to chaperones and optogenetics. These are judgments about category assignment, not eligibility exclusions.
4. **How informative is a Lasker award about the timing of a Nobel?** A historical audit showed that it is useful validation but does not establish an imminent Nobel or provide a clean forward probability.

The Nobel Foundation's selection description says recommendations are presented in September, the final selection occurs by vote, and nomination/evaluation documents remain confidential for 50 years. Thus, proximity to the announcement does not reveal the committee's preferences. Recent external awards are scientific-validation signals, not evidence of a disclosed Nobel shortlist. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2025/04/annual-review-2024.pdf?utm_source=openai))

## 2. Historical reference class—and its limitations

I audited **all 26 Medicine Nobel award years from 2000 through 2025**, matching official discoveries and laureates against earlier-announced **Basic or Clinical Lasker awards**. Public Service and Special Achievement awards were excluded, as were awards for substantively different work. The unit is an award year, not a scientist. These are historical records examined at the forecast cutoff, not preserved snapshots of the original webpages. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/all/?utm_source=openai))

The broad result was **17/26 = 65.3846%** with at least one qualifying same-discovery Lasker connection. However, the client's resolution rule requires a further adjustment for divided prizes. In 2008, the qualifying Lasker connection concerned HIV rather than first-listed HPV; in 2011 it concerned dendritic cells rather than first-listed innate immunity; in 2015 it concerned malaria rather than first-listed roundworm-parasite therapy. Applying the equal-share/first-discovery rule removes those three years, leaving **14/26 = 53.8462%**. The official historical motivations establish these distinctions; prize-share information was also checked in the Nobel API. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/2009-2000/?gallery_style=page&utm_source=openai))

For reproducibility, the remaining Nobel-year/earliest-Lasker-lag pairs, with lag measured in calendar years, are: **2000/17, 2001/3, 2003/19, 2005/10, 2007/6, 2009/3, 2010/9, 2012/3, 2013/11, 2018/3, 2019/3, 2020/20, 2023/2, and 2024/16**. The other 12 years have no qualifying dominant-discovery connection under this definition. Kandel's molecular-memory Lasker versus the broader 2000 signal-transduction Nobel is a boundary case; excluding it reduces the result to **13/26 = 50.0000%**.

Only **one of the 26 Nobel years** contained any qualifying same-year Lasker: Südhof in 2013. That year's earliest relevant Lasker was nevertheless 2002, for Rothman and Schekman. The distinction matters: neither a newly awarded Lasker nor a long wait after one is a reliable timing rule.

**These are backward-looking overlap rates, not P(Nobel | Lasker).** The necessary denominator of all eligible Lasker-recognized discoveries is absent. Nor does a Nobel without a prior Lasker imply Other: several supplied options are supported by other awards. I used this audit to avoid overconfidence and recency bias, not as a mechanical probability conversion.

## 3. Assessment of the twelve listed discoveries

### GLP-1: strongest named candidate

The **2024 Lasker Clinical award** recognized Habener, Mojsov, and Knudsen for discovery and development of GLP-1-based obesity therapies. The **2025 Breakthrough Prize** recognized Drucker, Habener, Holst, Knudsen, and Mojsov for the complementary discovery-to-treatment story. These establish unusually strong convergence around both foundational physiology and transformative medical application. The different recipient lists do not penalize this option under the client's semantics. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/))

My inference is that GLP-1 has the clearest combination of established discovery, broad clinical importance, and recent high-level recognition among the named choices. Nevertheless, those awards are correlated judgments from the scientific community, not independent committee endorsements. A compelling case for eventual recognition is not a compelling case for a majority probability in this particular year.

### Orexin: strongest recent positive update

The **2026 Lasker Basic award** recognized Mignot and Yanagisawa for identifying orexin's role in maintaining wakefulness and linking orexin deficiency to narcolepsy. The same underlying discovery had already received the **2023 Breakthrough Prize**. This is not merely a promising drug-development topic; it is an established physiological mechanism with a clear disease connection. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/orexin-a-brain-peptide-that-maintains-wakefulness/))

Crucially, the FDA's **August 5, 2026** release announced approval of **Orzeyful/oveporexton**, which directly activates the orexin pathway to treat adult narcolepsy type 1. This resolves stale descriptions that still characterize the approach as only investigational. FDA approval and commercial availability are not identical—the release also discusses subsequent controlled-substance scheduling—but the clinical validation is already present. I consequently rank orexin second among the listed discoveries. I do not treat the September Lasker as a guarantee of an October Nobel. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms))

### Chaperone-mediated protein folding

Hartl and Horwich's **2011 Lasker Basic award** recognized cellular machinery that assists proteins in reaching their functional forms. This is a mature, foundational biological discovery with a relatively coherent central attribution. I give it substantial probability even without a new 2026 catalyst. My principal discounts are competition from other basic-biology discoveries and uncertainty over Medicine versus Chemistry assignment. A long wait is not, by itself, evidence that the committee is now obliged to act. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/))

### Unfolded protein response

Mori and Walter's **2014 Lasker Basic award** recognized the mechanism by which cells detect problematic unfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum and initiate corrective responses. This is distinct from chaperones directly assisting folding; I did not merge the two options. Its fundamental cellular importance supports a meaningful probability. I place it below chaperones because my judgment gives slightly greater weight to the latter's foundational folding discovery, while both face a crowded cellular-mechanism field. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/))

### Optogenetics

The **2021 Lasker Basic award** recognized light-sensitive microbial proteins and their use in controlling neuronal activity. This supports Nobel-scale significance as an experimental method. The Lasker recipient list differs from the option's list, but that is not a resolution obstacle. I retain meaningful probability while discounting category competition and the possibility that the committee prefers a physiological discovery or a more direct therapeutic transformation this year. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/light-sensitive-microbial-proteins-optogenetics/))

### CAR-T therapy

June and Sadelain received the **2024 Breakthrough Prize**, announced on September 14, 2023, for engineering T cells with chimeric antigen receptors to attack cancer. The official account describes durable success against several blood cancers. This is a strong clinical-transformation candidate. My probability is restrained by competition from GLP-1 and multiple unlisted therapeutic discoveries, and by ambiguity between a specifically CAR-T motivation and broader adoptive-cell-therapy recognition. I did not assume that CAR-T had received a 2024 Lasker award. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/83))

### PCSK9

Hobbs's **2016 Breakthrough Prize** citation recognized human genetic variants affecting cholesterol and other lipids and their implications for treatment. The target-validation story is particularly attractive: protective human genetic variation helps identify a therapeutic strategy. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/2/L169))

A news lead prompted an additional primary-source check: FDA's notable-approvals table records **Lipfendra/enlicitide on July 16, 2026**, and its **July 17, 2026** news release describes the first oral PCSK9 inhibitor. I treat the one-day difference as approval date versus release date, not contradictory evidence. This gave PCSK9 a modest upward adjustment. It is an extension of an already validated target, however, not an entirely new discovery that should dominate the forecast. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/notable-approvals-drugs))

### Next-generation sequencing

The **2026 Princess of Asturias award** recognizes Klenerman, Balasubramanian, and Mayer for next-generation sequencing; its official account also documents their 2022 Breakthrough and 2024 Gairdner recognition. Scientific importance is not the limiting factor. I assign a low Medicine probability primarily because a Chemistry award is a plausible alternative for a sequencing methodology. ([fpa.es](https://www.fpa.es/en/princess-of-asturias-awards/laureates/2026-david-klenerman-shankar-balasubramanian-pascal-mayer/?texto=trayectoria))

The Wolf Foundation's current page additionally labels this work **Chemistry 2026**. Because that announcement is dated October 1 without a verified publication hour relative to the cutoff, I did not grant it an additional same-day momentum boost. It is corroborative of category ambiguity, not decisive Nobel evidence. ([wolffund.org.il](https://wolffund.org.il/shankar-balasubramanian/?utm_source=openai))

### Wnt signaling and organoids

Gairdner's account of Nusse's work connects Wnt signaling to development, cancer, adult stem-cell control, and organoid cultivation. This is an extensive and consequential biological program. My smaller probability reflects judgment about whether the committee would select this particular combined framing rather than another developmental or stem-cell discovery. An award for a different pathway would not match merely because it also concerns cell fate. ([gairdner.org](https://www.gairdner.org/winner/roel-nusse))

### Leptin and body-weight regulation

The **2010 Lasker Basic award** recognized Coleman and Friedman for leptin and the hormonal regulation of appetite and body weight. The discovery is foundational and remains a legitimate candidate. I place it below GLP-1 because the latter presently offers a stronger combined physiology-and-treatment narrative. That comparative discount is an inference, not a claim that leptin's importance has disappeared or that precise named laureates must match. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/leptin-a-hormone-that-regulates-appetite-and-body-weight/))

### Anti-TNF therapy

Feldmann and Maini received the **2003 Lasker Clinical award** for anti-TNF treatment of rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases. This is mature, consequential translational research. I retain a nontrivial probability but judge its current selection momentum weaker than the leading clinical alternatives. I impose neither an age-based exclusion nor an assumption that overdue recognition becomes inevitable. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/anti-tnf-for-treating-rheumatoid-arthritis/))

### Inherited breast/ovarian cancer susceptibility

King's Gairdner citation explicitly recognizes the discovery of inherited breast-cancer susceptibility through BRCA1. This is a strong discovery-based candidate, regardless of the eventual mix of laureates. I give it a smaller but meaningful allocation because my overall assessment favors the leading physiological, proteostasis, and therapeutic candidates—not because hereditary cancer genetics lacks Nobel significance. ([gairdner.org](https://www.gairdner.org/winner/mary-claire-king))

## 4. Why Other receives 33%

The supplied list is not an official shortlist. My specialist screen found several omitted discoveries with substantial primary-source validation:

- **cGAS/cytosolic DNA sensing:** the 2024 Lasker Basic award to James Chen, supporting a major innate-immunity discovery. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/))
- **Acute promyelocytic leukemia mechanism and targeted differentiation therapy:** the 2026 Shaw Life Science and Medicine award, announced May 27, to Anne Dejean, Hugues de Thé, and Zhu Chen. This offers a particularly coherent mechanism-to-treatment narrative. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/in/news-releases/announcement-of-the-shaw-laureates-2026-302782961.html))
- **Fetal-to-adult hemoglobin switching/BCL11A:** the April 18, 2026 Breakthrough announcement recognizes Orkin and Thein for elucidating the switch and validating it as a therapeutic target. The same release recognizes RPE65 gene therapy for inherited retinal degeneration—another unlisted medical discovery. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/98))
- **Notch signaling and CFTR-directed treatment:** the April 11, 2025 Gairdner announcement recognizes these separately. The 2025 Lasker Clinical award further validates cystic-fibrosis triple-drug therapy. Neither should automatically be absorbed into Wnt or general chaperone biology. ([gairdner.org](https://www.gairdner.org/resource-hub/2025-canada-gairdner-award-winners))
- **B/T lymphocyte lineages and TOR growth regulation:** mature, unlisted discoveries recognized by the 2019 and 2017 Lasker Basic awards, respectively. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/b-and-t-cells-the-organizing-principle-of-the-adaptive-immune-system/))
- **Phase separation and low-complexity protein domains:** additional cellular-organization contenders. I use the dated 2023 Breakthrough announcement for phase separation and the 2025 Lasker record for low-complexity domains, rather than interpreting inconsistent current directory labels as a fresh 2026 award. These subjects also face Chemistry competition. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/73))

I do not add these as independent probabilities: some overlap scientifically, and some may be more naturally rewarded in Chemistry. Nevertheless, their breadth materially increased my Other allocation from an initial **27% to 33%**. That adjustment rests particularly on the omitted APL, hemoglobin-switching, Notch, and CFTR evidence—not on mechanically adopting the specialist's suggested probability.

I excluded regulatory-T-cell/peripheral-tolerance work from the live candidate pool because it already won the **2025 Medicine Nobel**. I also avoided imposing a rigid field rotation: the 2025 immunology prize modestly affects my judgment about another immediately adjacent award, but does not rule one out. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2025/10/press-medicineprize2025.pdf?utm_source=openai))

## 5. Numerical construction

This is a **structured judgment forecast**, not a statistically fitted or historically validated thirteen-category model. To make the numerical choices reproducible, I first constructed three distributions representing alternative committee emphases: clinical transformation, foundational biology, and a less-publicized discovery. Their subjective weights were **40%, 40%, and 20%**, respectively. Each column below sums to 100%; none represents an observed committee preference.

| Discovery | Clinical emphasis, % | Foundational emphasis, % | Less-publicized emphasis, % | Initial blended weight |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GLP-1 | 36 | 12 | 12 | 21.6 |
| Optogenetics | 4 | 8 | 4 | 5.6 |
| CAR-T | 8 | 4 | 3 | 5.4 |
| Unfolded protein response | 3.5 | 10 | 4 | 6.2 |
| PCSK9 | 4.5 | 1.5 | 2 | 2.8 |
| Next-generation sequencing | 1 | 3 | 1.5 | 1.9 |
| Orexin | 12 | 11 | 7 | 10.6 |
| Wnt/organoids | 1.5 | 4.5 | 2 | 2.8 |
| Leptin | 1.5 | 3.5 | 1.5 | 2.3 |
| Anti-TNF | 3 | 1.5 | 1.5 | 2.1 |
| Chaperones | 6 | 14 | 5 | 9.0 |
| BRCA susceptibility | 3 | 2.5 | 2.5 | 2.7 |
| Other | 16 | 24.5 | 54 | 27.0 |

The initial blend already incorporates the orexin findings. After the broader candidate audit, I fixed **P(Other) = 0.33**. Following the additional FDA verification, I increased PCSK9's dimensionless allocation weight from **2.8 to 3.8**. All other listed weights remained unchanged. The twelve final listed weights sum to **74.0**.

The final calculation is therefore:

**P(listed discovery i) = 0.67 × weight_i / 74.0; P(Other) = 0.33.**

For example, GLP-1 is **0.67 × 21.6 / 74 = 0.1955675676**, orexin is **0.67 × 10.6 / 74 = 0.0959729730**, and PCSK9 is **0.67 × 3.8 / 74 = 0.0344054054**. I performed the calculations in Python and checked the reported values using decimal arithmetic. Rounding to four decimal places produces a sum of **exactly 1.0000**, without a residual adjustment.

## 6. Uncertainty and sensitivity

The main uncertainty is hidden committee preference, followed by shortlist incompleteness and category assignment. Repeated external awards are correlated, historical matching involves judgment, and current historical webpages are not original-publication snapshots. I have not treated award bodies' lifetime Nobel-conversion publicity as a one-year winning probability.

As a sensitivity check—not a confidence interval—holding the listed relative weights fixed while moving Other from **25% to 45%** changes GLP-1 from **21.8919% to 16.0541%**, orexin from **10.7432% to 7.8784%**, and chaperones from **9.1216% to 6.6892%**. Changing the committee-emphasis assumptions could move them further. Small differences between unfolded protein response, optogenetics, and CAR-T should not be interpreted as strong distinctions.

**The four decimal places express arithmetic consistency, not four-decimal predictive confidence.** My substantive conclusion is that GLP-1 leads the named candidates, orexin has received an important recent strengthening, and the omitted field remains large enough that Other is the largest single outcome.

Public awards establish scientific stature, not the winner of a confidential selection process ([Nobel selection rules](https://www.nobelprize.org/nomination/medicine/)).

## Context
This forecast uses the client’s October 1, 2026, 22:49 UTC cutoff. The announcement is scheduled for October 5, 2026, at 11:30 CEST at the earliest, equivalent to 09:30 UTC; it remains a future event ([official calendar](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates/)). Earlier scientific awards and regulatory decisions are evidence, not resolving events. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates?sm_guid=Mjk3MzM1fDI0MDExMjE4fC0xfHJzaGFsZXR0QHJlc2VhcmNoYW1lcmljYS5vcmd8MjM3MTYzMXx8MHwwfDMwMjE2OTQ3NXw5NTN8MHwwfHwyNjI2NDR8MA2&utm_source=openai))

Under the question’s rules, the discovery determines resolution, not the exact laureate roster. A divided prize is assigned by total discovery share, then announcement order if shares are equal. Attribution still matters indirectly: the Nobel permits no more than three recipients and generally excludes posthumous awards ([Nobel statutes](https://www.nobelprize.org/statutes-of-the-nobel-foundation/)).

## Evidence
The historical backbone argues against treating a recent precursor prize as an answer key. I audited Basic Lasker recipients against same-year Medicine Nobel recipients across 2000–2025, using official records retrieved for this assessment. There were 25 eligible Lasker cycles and 55 recipient slots; the awards were cancelled in 2020. Only one cycle had a same-year recipient overlap: Thomas Südhof in 2013, giving a cycle-level frequency of 1/25, or 4% ([Lasker recent archive](https://laskerfoundation.org/award/basic/), [older archive](https://laskerfoundation.org/award/basic/page/2/), [Nobel records](https://api.nobelprize.org/2.1/nobelPrizes?nobelPrizeYear=2000&yearTo=2025&nobelPrizeCategory=med&limit=50), [cancellation statement](https://laskerfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/03/2020_awards_cancellation_press_release.pdf)). This is a person-overlap reference class, not a fitted probability for the discovery in this question. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/award/basic/))

The full audited history is below. Counts refer to people, not discoveries; all rows use the official archives and Nobel records linked above.
