This does not cap orexin’s probability at the historical frequency. It shows that the same-year Lasker adds much less calendar information than its reputation suggests. Looking backward from Nobel winners to any earlier Lasker answers a different question and cannot supply a candidate’s forward annual probability.

GLP-1 has the strongest cumulative recognition sequence among the listed discoveries. Its hormone-to-treatment pathway received the 2024 Clinical Lasker, the April 5, 2025 Breakthrough Prize, and September 17, 2026 Clarivate recognition. These awards establish both foundational physiology and therapeutic importance; I count them as correlated assessments of one achievement, not independent evidence of the Nobel decision ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/), [Breakthrough](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/91), [Clarivate](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/)). ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/))

Its main weakness is credit allocation. The Lasker selected Habener, Mojsov, and Knudsen; Breakthrough recognized those researchers plus Drucker and Holst; Clarivate selected Drucker, Holst, and Mojsov. Habener died on December 28, 2025, leaving several substantial living contributors competing for the available recipient places. This complicates the award but does not disqualify the discovery ([Lasker roster](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/), [Breakthrough roster](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/91), [Clarivate roster](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/), [National Academy of Sciences record](https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/joel-f-habener-jpqij9/)).

Orexin has the strongest fresh challenger evidence. The September 9, 2026 Lasker announcement recognized Mignot and Yanagisawa for the wakefulness mechanism and the link between orexin deficiency and narcolepsy. FDA’s August 5, 2026 announcement for oveporexton adds direct therapeutic validation of that pathway. I read this as a compelling physiology–disease–treatment case, but the historical audit prevents the September award from dominating the forecast ([Lasker announcement](https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1143234), [scientific account](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/orexin-a-brain-peptide-that-maintains-wakefulness/), [FDA announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms)). ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/orexin-a-brain-peptide-that-maintains-wakefulness/))

Other contains identifiable competitors, not just an allowance for surprises. DNA sensing combines Chen’s 2024 Basic Lasker with the 2026 Japan Prize for Akira and Chen. OCT combines the 2023 Clinical Lasker with 2026 Clarivate recognition. A further omission is acute promyelocytic leukemia: the May 27, 2026 Shaw announcement recognized its molecular basis and targeted combination treatment, following the same team’s 2018 Sjöberg recognition. This last finding strengthens the outside-list allocation ([cGAS Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/), [Japan Prize](https://www.japanprize.jp/en/prize_past_2026_prize02.html), [OCT Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/optical-coherence-tomography/), [Clarivate](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/), [Shaw recognition](https://academie-sciences.fr/en/anne-dejean-hugues-de-and-zhu-chen-receive-shaw-prize), [Sjöberg recognition](https://www.kva.se/nyheter/sjobergpriset-2018/)). ([academie-sciences.fr](https://academie-sciences.fr/en/anne-dejean-hugues-de-and-zhu-chen-receive-shaw-prize))

The omitted pool also includes TOR growth regulation, integrins, epigenetics/Rett syndrome, and gene-replacement or hemoglobin-switching discoveries. Their combined weight matters even without any one becoming the favorite ([TOR](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/nutrient-activated-tor-proteins-that-regulate-cell-growth/), [integrins](https://laskerfoundation.org/award/basic/), [2026 Horwitz announcement](https://www.cuimc.columbia.edu/news/2026-horwitz-prize-awarded-work-epigenetics-neurological-diseases), [2026 Breakthrough announcement](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/98)).

I translated the evidence into the following relative scores. They combine scientific importance, maturity, Medicine-category fit, attribution, established recognition, and bounded updates for fresh evidence. They are judgmental weights, not measured nomination counts or empirical likelihood ratios.

| Discovery | Relative score | Main assessment |
|---|---:|---|
| GLP-1 | 22.5 | Strongest cumulative discovery-to-treatment case; attribution discount. |
| Orexin | 12.5 | Strong fresh physiological and therapeutic validation. |
| CAR-T | 6.8 | Recent cellular-immunotherapy recognition; TIL-versus-CAR-T motivation risk ([Tang Prize](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097)). |
| Optogenetics | 6.3 | Transformative neuroscience method; broad credit history ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/light-sensitive-microbial-proteins-optogenetics/)). |
| Chaperone folding | 6.0 | Mature basic discovery; fresh Hartl recognition modestly strengthens it ([Keio announcement](https://www.keio.ac.jp/en/press-release/20260918-press-01/)). |
| Unfolded protein response | 5.5 | Clear fundamental mechanism and compact attribution ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/)). |
| PCSK9 | 2.8 | Strong genetics-to-treatment case; oral-drug milestone adds a small update ([FDA](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-oral-pcsk9-inhibitor-lower-ldl-cholesterol-adults-high-cholesterol)). |
| Next-generation sequencing | 2.7 | Enormous methodological impact; Chemistry is a competing home in my assessment ([Asturias recognition](https://www.fpa.es/en/princess-of-asturias-awards/laureates/2026-david-klenerman-shankar-balasubramanian-pascal-mayer/?texto=acta)). |
| Wnt/organoids | 2.5 | Important biology; less unified potential motivation ([Clevers recognition](https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/2/L29)). |
| Leptin | 2.5 | Landmark physiology; weaker current comparative case than GLP-1 ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/leptin-a-hormone-that-regulates-appetite-and-body-weight/)). |
| Inherited cancer susceptibility | 2.5 | Durable clinical impact; credit spans mapping and gene identification ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/breast-cancer-genetics-and-human-rights/)). |
| Anti-TNF | 1.8 | Established therapeutic achievement; age of recognition is neither a veto nor an overdue bonus ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/anti-tnf-for-treating-rheumatoid-arthritis/)). |
| Other | 30.0 | Multiple strong omitted discoveries plus unobserved alternatives. |

The scores total 104.4. I calculate each probability as \(p_i=w_i/\sum_j w_j\), where \(w_i\) is its relative score, then use sum-preserving rounding. The output decimals preserve the calculation; they do not imply equivalent precision about secret deliberations. No prediction-market prices or betting odds enter the estimate.

## What's non-obvious
The exact scientist combinations in the options are not eligibility tests. Attribution complexity can delay selection, but a different GLP-1 roster still matches GLP-1 under this question. The reverse matters for CAR-T: a broad cellular-immunotherapy award dominated by tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte work could resolve to Other, despite overlapping scientists. The recent Tang citation explicitly encompasses both approaches ([Tang motivation](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097)).

Orexin’s regulatory milestone is also narrower than an uncomplicated “drug launched” narrative. FDA publicly announced approval, but its letter ties the statutory approval date and marketing permission to DEA scheduling. I count this as regulatory validation, not proof of widespread treatment availability by the cutoff ([FDA announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms), [approval letter](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220860Orig1s000ltr.pdf)). ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/2026/220860Orig1s000ltr.pdf))

## Uncertainties
The decisive missing evidence is the confidential evaluation of nominees. Nobel records remain secret for 50 years, so public honors cannot establish the current shortlist or vote ([selection rules](https://www.nobelprize.org/nomination/medicine/)). I give little weight to committee members’ specialties or public lectures: they show scientific visibility, not a verified selection signal ([committee leadership](https://www.karolinska.se/om-oss/centrala-nyheter/2026/01/karolinska-medarbetare-blir-ny-ordforande-for-nobelkommitten/), [Mojsov lecture](https://news.ki.se/svetlana-mojsov-to-deliver-this-years-nicholson-lecture-on-3-june)).

Category allocation and official wording remain material risks. The protein-quality-control candidates are distinct from the computational design and structure-prediction work rewarded in Chemistry, so I do not treat them as already awarded ([2024 Chemistry motivation](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/b/)). I also impose no automatic field rotation after the immune-tolerance prize ([2025 Medicine motivation](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2025/popular-information/)).

My calculated sensitivity checks show the model’s limits: varying only GLP-1’s score by 30% in either direction gives probabilities of 16–26%; varying orexin’s by 40% gives 8–16%; varying Other’s by 25% gives 23–33.5%. These are scenario ranges from the scores above, not statistical confidence intervals. Access to the actual nomination pool, scientific evaluations, and proposed motivation would narrow uncertainty far more than another public award announcement.

## Forecast as of October 1, 2026, 22:34 UTC

### Bottom line

My highest-probability **individual listed discovery** is **orexin and sleep–wake regulation** at 19.2%, narrowly ahead of **GLP-1 biology and therapeutics** at 16.8%. However, **Other** is the largest category at 30.1% because it aggregates several serious omitted candidates—notably cGAS–STING innate-DNA sensing and optical coherence tomography—plus the normal possibility of a less-publicized Nobel choice.

No option approaches 50%. Nobel nominations and evaluations are secret, and public precursor awards identify a pool of Nobel-class discoveries much better than they predict the exact award year.

## 1. Institutional and historical prior

Medicine nominations were due January 31, evaluations were scheduled through August, the committee recommendation followed in September, and the Nobel Assembly votes in October. Nominations and deliberations remain confidential for 50 years. Consequently, September awards such as the Lasker and Clarivate recognitions can indicate independent scientific convergence, but they are not evidence of a leaked shortlist and generally arrived too late to determine who was nominated. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/themes/the-nobel-prize-in-physiology-or-medicine-1901-2000/?utm_source=openai))

The maximum of three laureates is an important constraint. Through 2025, Medicine had 40 one-person prizes, 36 two-person prizes, and 40 three-person prizes. Discoveries with a clean two- or three-person attribution therefore receive a modest advantage over fields with five or more defensible claimants. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/facts-on-the-nobel-prize-in-physiology-or-medicine/?utm_source=openai))

I matched 180 person-award records from the 1980–2025 Lasker Basic and Clinical awards against subsequent or same-year Medicine Nobels. Fifty-two, or 28.9%, eventually matched a Medicine laureate; the rate was about 40.6% for Basic recipients and 13.9% for Clinical recipients. Among those 52 matches, only eight were same-year, while 20 occurred after one to three years. The matched lag had a three-year median. This is a person-level, right-censored base rate—not a direct annual probability—but it argues against treating the September 2026 Lasker as a same-year oracle. The underlying award histories come from the Lasker archive and official Nobel records. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/?utm_source=openai))

The lag pattern modestly favors discoveries recognized by a Lasker two to five years ago—GLP-1 in 2024, optical coherence tomography in 2023, and optogenetics in 2021—over very old unawarded Lasker fields. It does not exclude long waits: several historical matches occurred more than 15 years later.

The 2025 prize concerned peripheral immune tolerance. Consecutive prizes in related fields are possible, but another immunology-centered choice would be a mild departure from the recent pattern. I therefore apply only a modest penalty—not a veto—to cGAS–STING, CAR-T, and anti-TNF. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2025/popular-information/?user_id=66c4c0b35d78644b3aac5919&utm_source=openai))

## 2. Leading listed options

### Orexin — 19.2%

The strongest recent evidence is the 2026 Lasker Basic Medical Research Award to Emmanuel Mignot and Masashi Yanagisawa for identifying orexin and establishing that orexin deficiency causes narcolepsy. The citation is unusually Nobel-ready: a fundamental physiological mechanism, a clear human disease, mature work dating to the late 1990s, and a compact recipient set. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/orexin-a-brain-peptide-that-maintains-wakefulness/?utm_source=openai))

The major weak-signal update is the FDA's August 5, 2026 approval of oveporexton, the first approved medicine directly restoring orexin signaling and targeting the underlying cause of narcolepsy type 1. This completes the discovery-to-mechanism-to-treatment arc before the Nobel committee's September recommendation. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms?utm_source=openai))

There is also a very small committee-composition signal: 2026 committee chair Per Svenningsson is a neurologist and vice chair Sten Linnarsson is a prominent neuroscience researcher. The full 50-member Assembly and ad hoc experts prevent this from carrying much weight, but it slightly strengthens neuroscience candidates such as orexin and optogenetics. ([karolinska.se](https://www.karolinska.se/om-oss/centrala-nyheter/2026/01/karolinska-medarbetare-blir-ny-ordforande-for-nobelkommitten/?utm_source=openai))

Reasons not to go higher include the low historical frequency of same-year Lasker-to-Nobel conversions and the competing credit claim of Luis de Lecea's independent hypocretin work. I treat the Lasker, FDA approval, and associated publicity as correlated evidence rather than three independent signals.

### GLP-1 — 16.8%

GLP-1 has the strongest combination of global medical impact and recent precursor recognition. The 2024 Clinical Lasker honored Joel Habener, Svetlana Mojsov, and Lotte Bjerre Knudsen for discovering the active hormone and developing obesity therapies. Its account also names Drucker, Holst, John Eng, Richard DiMarchi, and others as important contributors. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/?utm_source=openai))

Clarivate's September 2026 group instead selected Daniel Drucker, Jens Juul Holst, and Mojsov for identifying and characterizing GLP-1 and its biological activity. Clarivate also emphasized that GLP-1 receptor agonists have transformed diabetes and obesity care for millions. ([clarivate.com](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/?utm_source=openai))

A notable but speculative local signal is that Mojsov gave the 2026 Nicholson Lecture on GLP-1 at Karolinska's Nobel Forum on June 3. This demonstrates strong local scientific salience but is not evidence that the Nobel Assembly had selected her. The lecture is part of an institutional exchange program and was public months before the announcement. I assign it only a very small positive weight. ([nyheter.ki.se](https://nyheter.ki.se/missa-inte-arets-nicholsonforelasning-med-svetlana-mojsov-den-3-juni?utm_source=openai))

The principal negative is attribution. The 2024 Lasker and 2026 Clarivate trios overlap only on Mojsov, and a broader recognition would contain more than three plausible living contributors. The Nobel Assembly could solve this by framing the prize narrowly around GLP-1 identification or around therapeutic development, but it could also postpone the subject rather than make a controversial exclusion.

## 3. Why Other remains 30.1%

The listed options omit multiple discoveries with evidence comparable to several named choices.

**cGAS–STING** is the strongest omitted contender in my assessment. Zhijian Chen received the 2024 Lasker Basic award for discovering cGAS and the cGAMP–STING DNA-sensing pathway. The field also received 2025 Clarivate recognition and a 2026 Japan Prize centered on nucleic-acid sensing. It has fundamental mechanism, broad relevance to infection, cancer, inflammation, and autoimmunity, and a Nobel-compatible three-person formulation. Its main negative is that it would produce a second consecutive immunology-related prize. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/?utm_source=openai))

**Optical coherence tomography** is another major omission. Fujimoto, Huang, and Swanson won the 2023 Clinical Lasker for a technology that revolutionized retinal imaging and were all named 2026 Clarivate Citation Laureates. It offers an exceptionally clean three-person configuration and fits the historical precedent of Medicine Nobels for CT and MRI. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/optical-coherence-tomography/?utm_source=openai))

The remaining Other probability covers discoveries such as B- and T-cell differentiation, mTOR signaling, ghrelin, biomolecular phase separation, immune-cell adhesion receptors, hemophilia bispecific antibodies, gene therapy, and possibilities not prominent in public prediction articles. Clarivate's 2026 Medicine selections themselves included two complete omitted clusters—OCT and Timothy Springer's immune-cell adhesion receptors—besides GLP-1. ([clarivate.com](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/?utm_source=openai))

My approximate internal decomposition of Other is about 6% for cGAS–STING, 5–6% for OCT, and roughly 18–19% spread across all remaining omitted discoveries. These are not separate resolution categories and therefore remain combined under Other.

Credit is less clean than it appears because different awards have substituted Miesenböck, Oesterhelt, Boyden, and other pioneers in the third slot. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/light-sensitive-microbial-proteins-optogenetics/?utm_source=openai))

([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/?utm_source=openai))

## 5. Weak signals and calibration

I explicitly investigated institutional calendars, recent award announcements, FDA decisions, committee composition, and public schedules. The useful weak signals were the orexin drug approval, Mojsov's Nobel Forum lecture, Hartl's new Keio Prize, and the neuroscience background of the 2026 committee leadership. None resembles a credible leak, and together they move probabilities by only a few percentage points.

After establishing the independent forecast, I checked for relevant active prediction markets. No usable market pricing for the discovery question was found, so there was no market-based adjustment.

The main calibration choice is keeping both leaders below 20% and retaining 30.1% for Other. Public Nobel predictions routinely understate the breadth of the candidate universe, and the actual nominations are unknowable until the 50-year confidentiality period expires. The final distribution therefore favors orexin and GLP-1 without treating either as close to certain.

## Summary and interpretation

**Forecast as of October 1, 2026, 22:34 UTC:** GLP-1 is my strongest individual discovery candidate, at **22.45%**. Nevertheless, **Other is the largest resolution category, at 29.025%**, because it combines several credible discoveries omitted from the shortlist. Orexin is my second-highest named option, at **11.425%**.

The official schedule places the Medicine announcement on **October 5, 2026, at 11:30 CEST at the earliest**, equivalent to 09:30 UTC. This forecast concerns that forthcoming announcement; earlier awards and clinical developments are evidence, not events that resolve the question. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates/?sm_guid=Mjk3MzM1fDI0MDExMjE4fC0xfHJzaGFsZXR0QHJlc2VhcmNoYW1lcmljYS5vcmd8MjM3MTYzMXx8MHwwfDI3NzgwMzExOHw5NTN8MHwwfHwyNjI2NDR8MA2&utm_source=openai))

I interpret the options as discovery categories, not exact laureate combinations or verbatim citation strings. Thus, a GLP-1 prize involving Daniel Drucker rather than Lotte Bjerre Knudsen could still resolve to GLP-1. Conversely, a prize involving June, Sadelain, and Rosenberg could resolve to Other if its principal discovery were tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy rather than CAR-T. Any divided prize must be assigned using the question’s discovery-share and announcement-order rules.

## Research approach and evidence limitations

I investigated four decision-relevant questions:

1. **Which discoveries have both established scientific importance and fresh recognition before the cutoff?** This particularly affects GLP-1, orexin, and CAR-T.
2. **Which candidates might instead receive the Chemistry prize?** This particularly affects sequencing and chaperone-assisted folding.
3. **Does the shortlist omit discoveries with equally strong credentials?** This determines the necessary size of Other.
4. **How informative are precursor awards about the particular year of a Nobel?** This prevents treating a recent Lasker or Citation Laureate designation as an answer key.

The principal evidence came from NobelPrize.org and its historical data service, the Lasker Foundation, the Breakthrough Prize Foundation, Clarivate’s own announcement, the Tang Prize Foundation, the Princess of Asturias Foundation, Columbia University, and the FDA. I also commissioned a comparative research review and a historical Nobel–Lasker crosswalk, then checked the most consequential findings against primary sources. I did **not** use prediction-market prices, betting odds, or public numerical forecast aggregates.

The critical limitation is that these are public signals of scientific readiness, not observations of the selection process. Nobel nomination information is confidential for 50 years. I have no verified information about the current nominations, shortlist, deliberations, or vote. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/nomination?trk=public_post_comment-text&utm_source=openai))

Dates below refer to the award year or dated announcement, not search-engine crawl dates or subsequent website edits. The historical calculations use records retrieved for this October 1, 2026 assessment. Awards are correlated indicators: multiple prizes recognizing the same work do not constitute independent experiments, and syndicated copies of an announcement were not counted as additional evidence.

## Historical calibration

An API-assisted, discovery-level crosswalk covered **26 annual Medicine prizes, 2000–2025 inclusive**. It identified a matching earlier Lasker Basic or Clinical award for **at least one Nobel-recognized discovery in 17 of 26 years**, or **65.3846%**. For the **2010–2025 subset**, the corresponding count was **10 of 16**, or **62.5%**. These are my calculations from the Nobel historical records and Lasker archive, not statistics published by either institution. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/about/developer-zone/?utm_source=openai))

For reproducibility, the positive Nobel-year → earliest matching Lasker-year pairs were: 2000→1983; 2001→1998; 2003→1984; 2005→1995; 2007→2001; 2008→1986; 2009→2006; 2010→2001; 2011→2007; 2012→2009; 2013→2002; 2015→2011; 2018→2015; 2019→2016; 2020→2000; 2023→2021; 2024→2008. The **17 observed earliest-award gaps** had a **median of six years**, ranging from **two to 22 years**. Matching involves judgment, and an unmatched year means no qualifying match was identified—not certified proof of absence. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/about/developer-zone/?utm_source=openai))

This exercise accepts a match to any discovery within a divided Nobel, unlike the client’s winner-selection rule, so it is background calibration only. My takeaway is modest: major precursor awards matter, but award timing is weak enough that several plausible candidates and omitted discoveries must retain substantial probability.

I used three deliberately different assessment lenses rather than pretending to have a statistically fitted model of confidential Nobel decisions:

The main uncertainties are unobserved selection preferences, attribution, Chemistry-versus-Medicine allocation, and the official motivation’s scope. I do not impose a deterministic rotation among fields or assume that recent public acclaim guarantees selection.

## 1. Interpretation of the resolution criteria

I forecast the **discovery in the official motivation**, not the exact recipient roster. Consequently, a GLP-1 award involving Daniel Drucker rather than one of the named scientists would still match the GLP-1 option. Likewise, a different optogenetics or CAR-T recipient configuration would not, by itself, cause resolution to Other.

I also distinguish this question from whether a discovery receives *any* 2026 Nobel recognition. A discovery recognized only by the Chemistry prize would not satisfy this Medicine question. If Medicine recognizes multiple discoveries, the client's largest-share/first-mentioned rule determines the result. Closely connected topics such as chaperone-assisted folding and the unfolded protein response therefore remain separate options; an eventual broad protein-quality-control motivation introduces some matching uncertainty.

The Nobel's maximum of three recipients matters indirectly. Complicated attribution can make a discovery harder to package into an award, even though recipient mismatch is not itself a resolution problem. The official rules also generally prohibit newly awarding a prize to someone already deceased. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/facts-on-the-nobel-prize-in-physiology-or-medicine/?utm_source=openai))

## 2. Research approach and evidence quality

I pursued four decision-relevant research threads:

1. **Does GLP-1 have substantive scientific and award recognition, rather than merely contemporary pharmaceutical visibility?**
2. **Has orexin acquired fresh recognition or clinical validation that changes its position?**
3. **Which outside-list discoveries justify substantial probability for Other?**
4. **How predictive should major precursor awards be, especially a same-year Lasker?**

The research combined primary award-provider pages, FDA announcements, institutional sources, a Nobel historical-data query, English- and Swedish-language news searches, two focused research reports, and a historical Nobel–Lasker comparison. The conclusions below rely principally on the underlying primary sources, not on the reports' qualitative rankings. I did not use prediction-market prices or betting odds.

For contemporary evidence, I checked the announcement date and award year rather than treating a recent crawl or ceremony as a new scientific honor. Historical award facts were retrieved in their current published form as of the cutoff; they are not reconstructed point-in-time candidate lists. Some official Nobel and Clarivate pages blocked direct opening, so their accessible official search extracts, other official pages, and the Nobel data query supplied the relevant information. Negative search findings are not treated as proof that a discovery lacks nominations or recognition.

## 3. The strongest positive case: GLP-1

### A concentrated recognition sequence

GLP-1 has a particularly strong sequence across successive award cycles:

- **2024 Lasker Clinical Award:** Joel Habener, Svetlana Mojsov, and Lotte Bjerre Knudsen were recognized for GLP-1 discovery and development into obesity treatment. The official account distinguishes identification of the active hormone from engineering useful medicines. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/))
- **April 5, 2025 Breakthrough Prize announcement:** Drucker, Habener, Holst, Knudsen, and Mojsov were jointly recognized for contributions spanning hormone discovery, physiological characterization, and therapeutic development. 
- **September 17, 2026 Clarivate Citation Laureates:** Drucker, Holst, and Mojsov were recognized for GLP-1 identification, characterization, and biological activity. This is a fresh, Medicine-specific recognition immediately preceding the Nobel announcement. ([clarivate.com](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/?utm_source=openai))

This is stronger evidence than commercial popularity alone. The Lasker scientific narrative traces the work back to the 1980s; GLP-1 is not an immature discovery simply because obesity medicines have recently become especially visible. Its combination of endocrine physiology and established therapeutic translation also gives it a natural Medicine-category fit. That category assessment is my inference from the recognized work, not evidence about the Nobel Assembly's actual preference. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/))

### Why I nevertheless keep GLP-1 below one-quarter

First, these recognitions are **correlated assessments of the same achievement**, not independent confirmations of a Nobel decision. Clarivate explicitly says its program does not predict recipients in a particular year. I therefore use its 2026 selection as a moderate update, not as a reliable same-year forecast. ([clarivate.com](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/?utm_source=openai))

Second, attribution remains complicated. Lasker selected three scientists, Breakthrough five, and the latest Clarivate recognition a different overlapping trio. The Nobel must select no more than three. Habener is also deceased: Johns Hopkins' institutional remembrance, published **April 20, 2026**, identifies his death as **December 28, 2025**. I use that chronology rather than inferring a death date from adjacent entries in a news archive. His death constrains the possible recipient configuration but does not disqualify GLP-1 as the discovery. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/))

Finally, Nobel-worthiness is not the same as winning in 2026. Several established basic discoveries remain credible alternatives, and no public evidence identifies the committee's actual shortlist.

The audit identified:

- **13/20 years, or 65%,** with at least one qualifying earlier Lasker recipient.
- **1/20 years, or 5%,** with a same-year match: Südhof in 2013. That year also had earlier Lasker matches, so the two counts overlap.

The earlier-match Nobel years were 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2015, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2023, and 2024. These counts were computed from the historical Nobel data query and named-recipient checks against the Lasker archive, using sources retrieved at the forecast cutoff. They describe at-least-one-laureate overlap, not necessarily the discovery that would prevail under this question's split-prize rule. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/all-awards-winners/))

Most importantly, **P(previous Lasker recognition | Nobel winner) is not P(Nobel winner | Lasker recognition)**. The latter requires the denominator of all recognized discoveries, including those never receiving a Nobel. I therefore use the audit only to support two restrained conclusions: precursor recognition is relevant, and a same-year Lasker should not be treated as an automatic immediate Nobel signal. I do not convert 65% or 5% into any candidate's probability.

## 8. Reproducible numerical construction

There is insufficient public information to fit a defensible statistical model of the confidential choice. I therefore use an explicitly judgmental categorical model, rather than presenting subjective assessments as measured likelihood ratios.

First, I assign a **reference distribution** using established scientific importance, recognition, attribution, Medicine-category fit, and competition from unlisted discoveries. Second, I apply relative evidence multipliers for the verified newer developments. Third, I retain 15% weight on the reference distribution to reduce dependence on recent-award salience.

| Discovery | Reference probability b | Evidence multiplier m |
|---|---:|---:|
| GLP-1 | 0.180 | 1.80 |
| Optogenetics | 0.080 | 1.00 |
| CAR-T | 0.070 | 1.00 |
| Unfolded protein response | 0.075 | 1.00 |
| PCSK9 | 0.035 | 1.00 |
| Next-generation sequencing | 0.030 | 1.25 |
| Orexin | 0.060 | 2.80 |
| Wnt/organoids | 0.035 | 1.00 |
| Leptin | 0.045 | 1.00 |
| TNF | 0.025 | 1.00 |
| Chaperone-mediated folding | 0.075 | 1.00 |
| BRCA susceptibility | 0.035 | 1.00 |
| Other | 0.255 | 1.35 |

These reference probabilities sum to 1. The multipliers are **elicited relative weights**, not empirically estimated Bayes factors. GLP-1 receives an uplift for its current recognition convergence; orexin receives a larger proportional uplift for the combination of new basic-research recognition and direct clinical validation; sequencing receives a small uplift for its verified 2026 honor; Other receives an uplift for the identifiable contemporary alternatives. A multiplier of 1 means no additional update—not that the discovery is weak or absent from consideration.

The calculation is:

**Z = Σ(bᵢmᵢ) = 1.34875**

**qᵢ = bᵢmᵢ / Z**

**pᵢ = 0.85qᵢ + 0.15bᵢ**

For example, GLP-1 is 0.85 × (0.180 × 1.80 / 1.34875) + 0.15 × 0.180 = **0.2311890639** before output rounding. The corresponding unrounded probabilities for orexin and Other are **0.1148758109** and **0.2552008804**.

I performed the normalization in Python. The output uses largest-remainder rounding in increments of **0.00001**, preserving a categorical total of exactly 1.00000.

## 9. Sensitivity and uncertainty

I tested all **81 combinations** of three alternative multiplier values for each updated category: GLP-1 {1.3, 1.8, 2.3}; orexin {1.6, 2.8, 4.0}; sequencing {1.0, 1.25, 1.5}; and Other {1.0, 1.35, 1.7}. Holding the reference distribution and mixture rule fixed, the resulting ranges were approximately:

- GLP-1: **16.6%–30.4%**.
- Orexin: **6.5%–17.4%**.
- Other: **19.0%–32.9%**.

These are **model-sensitivity ranges, not statistical confidence intervals**. Varying the reference weights themselves would widen uncertainty further. The five decimal places in the final object make the arithmetic reproducible; they do not imply that the confidential decision can be forecast to five-decimal accuracy.

The principal conclusion is consequently restrained: **GLP-1 is the best-supported individual choice, orexin has the strongest fresh challenger evidence, and the collective outside-list probability remains substantial.**

## Forecast summary

**GLP-1 is my leading individual discovery, at 21.0719595%. Other is the largest category, at 27.2294033%, because it contains numerous credible discoveries rather than one competing research program.** Among the remaining listed discoveries, I put orexin first, followed by the unfolded protein response, CAR-T therapy, chaperone-assisted folding, and optogenetics.

This forecast uses an information cutoff of **October 1, 2026, 22:34 UTC**. The official announcement is scheduled for **October 5, 2026, at 11:30 CEST at the earliest**, equivalent to 09:30 UTC—82 hours and 56 minutes after the cutoff. This remains a forecast of a future announcement; earlier scientific discoveries, awards, and regulatory decisions are background evidence, not resolving events. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates/?sm_guid=Mjk3MzM1fDI0MDExMjE4fC0xfHJzaGFsZXR0QHJlc2VhcmNoYW1lcmljYS5vcmd8MjM3MTYzMXx8MHwwfDI5NzY0NzA3MXw5NTN8MHwwfHwyNjI2NDR8MA2&utm_source=openai))

## 1. Interpretation and research method

I forecast the **discovery that determines resolution**, not the exact laureate roster. A GLP-1 award to Drucker, Holst, and Mojsov would count for the GLP-1 option despite differing from its named trio. For a divided prize, shares must be aggregated by discovery; the largest individual laureate share is not necessarily the largest discovery share. Equal discovery shares are resolved by announcement order, as specified in the question. I therefore do not assign overlapping YES probabilities to discoveries that might appear together.

The central limitation is institutional opacity. Nobel nomination and evaluation information is confidential for at least 50 years. Public prize recognition can establish scientific stature, but cannot establish that a discovery is on the committee's current shortlist. Nobel rules also limit an award to three people and prohibit ordinary posthumous awards, making attribution relevant without requiring the roster in an option to match. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/statutes-of-the-nobel-foundation/?utm_source=openai))

I retrieved historical Medicine awards for **2000–2025 inclusive, N = 26 annual prizes**, through the Nobel-data MCP; examined primary records from Nobel, Lasker, Gairdner, Breakthrough, FDA, and other award institutions; and used date-constrained Perigon news searches to corroborate recent developments. Two focused research briefs helped audit the Lasker base rate and compare scientific contributions. I used their sourced evidence, not their proposed probability allocations. I did not use prediction-market prices, betting odds, or public forecast aggregates. I examined Clarivate's citation-based recognition only after constructing an initial independent allocation.

The historical records show that Medicine recognizes both fundamental mechanisms and clinical advances. Recent examples include microRNA in 2024, peripheral immune tolerance in 2025, and vaccine-enabling RNA modifications in 2023. Consequently, I do not require a blockbuster treatment for a discovery to be competitive, and I do not impose a mechanical rule that immunology cannot win after an immunology year. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/laureates/?utm_source=openai))

## 2. Decision-relevant research threads

### A. Does the fresh orexin Lasker make orexin the overwhelming favorite?

**No, but it warrants a substantial upward update.** The 2026 Lasker Basic award recognizes Mignot and Yanagisawa for identifying orexin and linking its deficiency to narcolepsy. The Foundation's media announcement was dated September 9, 2026. This is a particularly coherent physiology-to-disease discovery, rather than recognition based only on publication volume. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/orexin-a-brain-peptide-that-maintains-wakefulness/?utm_source=openai))

I specifically investigated the forward-looking, same-year precedent instead of using the often-cited eventual overlap between Lasker and Nobel winners. The audit covered **Lasker Basic award years 2000–2025**, excluding **2020**, when the awards were cancelled: **25 award cycles and 55 recipient slots**. Only **one cycle**, 2013, contained a recipient who also received that year's Medicine Nobel: Thomas Südhof. Thus the award-cycle overlap was **1/25 = 4.0%**. This is a recipient-overlap proxy, not a fitted probability for discovery matching, but it strongly cautions against treating a September Lasker as an automatic October Nobel signal. The audit is reproducible by joining each year's Basic recipients to that year's official Medicine laureates; all cycles other than 2013 have zero same-year recipient overlap. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/all-awards-winners/))

A second, independently important development strengthens orexin's scientific case: **FDA approved oveporexton, marketed as Orzeyful, on August 5, 2026**, for adults with narcolepsy type 1. Its mechanism restores orexin signaling, directly connecting the original discovery to treatment of the underlying biological deficit. I therefore give orexin more than a recognition-only update, while keeping its final probability below 8%. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms?utm_source=openai))

### B. Is GLP-1's prominence supported by Nobel-shaped science and demonstrated medical benefit?

**Yes.** The 2024 Lasker Clinical award recognized Mojsov, Habener, and Knudsen for the hormone-to-drug pathway. The 2025 Breakthrough award recognized five contributors—Drucker, Habener, Holst, Knudsen, and Mojsov—covering hormone identification, physiology, and therapeutic development. These records support both fundamental novelty and translation, rather than merely commercial success. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/))

The clinical case also extends beyond weight loss: FDA approved Wegovy's cardiovascular-risk-reduction indication on **March 8, 2024**, for adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity. That is evidence of consequential health-outcome benefit, not simply attention surrounding popular medicines. ([accessdata.fda.gov](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2024/215256Orig1s011.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Recognition continued during 2026. Mojsov shared the Broermann award announced on **July 14, 2026**; and Clarivate's **September 17, 2026** release recognized Drucker, Holst, and Mojsov for GLP-1 identification, characterization, and biological activity. Clarivate explicitly says its program is not intended to predict recipients in a particular year. I treat this as corroborating evidence of research influence, not as a probability forecast, and assume the various recognitions are positively correlated. ([lmu.de](https://www.lmu.de/en/newsroom/news-overview/news/lmu-president-receives-one-of-the-worlds-most-prestigious-medical-science-awards-f90d0674.html))

The principal counterweight is credit allocation. The five-person Breakthrough roster exceeds Nobel's three-person limit. Habener died on **December 28, 2025**, so he cannot receive an ordinary new Nobel. However, I do **not** treat GLP-1 as disqualified: surviving researchers have substantial, distinct contributions, and this question matches discoveries rather than the listed names. Attribution complexity merits a modest discount, not elimination. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/91))

### C. Did the 2024 Chemistry prize already dispose of the protein-folding candidates?

**No.** That prize recognized computational protein design and protein-structure prediction. It did not recognize the cellular machinery that assists folding or the signaling system that responds to misfolded proteins. I therefore retain meaningful probabilities for both chaperones and UPR, rather than treating them as already awarded. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/b/?utm_source=openai))

UPR has a particularly clean major-award attribution structure: Mori and Walter shared the 2014 Lasker Basic award for identifying the ER quality-control response. Hartl and Horwich shared the 2011 Basic award for chaperone-assisted folding. My slight preference for UPR is a judgment about the specificity of its physiological signaling mechanism and Medicine framing—not evidence of committee preference. Both remain strong, mature fundamental-discovery candidates. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/))

### D. Is Other a genuine contender pool or merely an uncertainty allowance?

It is a genuine contender pool. Important examples include:

- **Nucleic-acid sensing/cGAS:** Chen received the 2024 Lasker Basic award; Akira and Chen were announced as 2026 Japan Prize recipients on January 21 for innate nucleic-acid sensing. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/))
- **TOR/mTOR nutrient sensing:** Hall's 2017 Lasker Basic award recognizes a central mechanism controlling cell growth. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/nutrient-activated-tor-proteins-that-regulate-cell-growth/))
- **CFTR-modulating treatment:** Welsh, González, and Negulescu received the 2025 Lasker Clinical award for triple-drug cystic-fibrosis therapy. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/combined-triple-drug-therapy-for-cystic-fibrosis/))
- **Epigenetic regulation and neurological disease:** Bird and Zoghbi received the 2026 Horwitz recognition announced September 2. ([cuimc.columbia.edu](https://www.cuimc.columbia.edu/news/2026-horwitz-prize-awarded-work-epigenetics-neurological-diseases))
- **Optical coherence tomography and immune adhesion receptors:** both were included alongside GLP-1 in Clarivate's September 2026 Medicine recognition. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs-302880553.html))
- **Gene therapy and hemoglobin switching:** the April 18, 2026 Breakthrough announcement recognized inherited-retinal gene therapy and the fetal-to-adult hemoglobin mechanism underlying treatments for sickle-cell disease and beta-thalassemia. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/98))
- **Protein aggregation and proteomics:** the 2026 Gairdner awards include Kelly's tafamidis work and methods underlying modern proteomics. ([gairdner.org](https://www.gairdner.org/resource-hub/2026-canada-gairdner-award-winners))

None needs to rival GLP-1 individually for their combined probability to exceed it. This breadth is why I resist allocating nearly all probability to the twelve supplied discoveries.

## 3. Candidate-by-candidate weighting inputs

I used a **transparent subjective weighting model**, not a statistically fitted Nobel-selection model. The baseline represents my comparative assessment of scientific importance, maturity, medical relevance, attribution manageability, and established recognition. The multiplier incorporates decision-relevant 2026 evidence. The factors are judgmental relative-weight adjustments, **not empirically estimated Bayesian likelihood ratios**.

|---|---:|---:|---|
| GLP-1 | 0.205 | 1.35 | Strong fundamental-to-clinical package; 2024 Lasker and 2025 Breakthrough underpin the baseline, with further 2026 recognition supporting a bounded update. Attribution remains the main concern. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/)) |
| Optogenetics | 0.070 | 1.00 | The 2021 Lasker Basic establishes field-transforming neuroscience importance. A strong method candidate, although I allow uncertainty about Nobel category and framing. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/light-sensitive-microbial-proteins-optogenetics/)) |
| CAR-T | 0.070 | 1.15 | The 2024 Breakthrough and Gairdner records support major therapeutic impact. The February 11, 2026 BBVA announcement adds current recognition, without making it decisive. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/83)) |
| UPR | 0.090 | 1.00 | Mature, general cellular mechanism with a compact two-person 2014 Lasker attribution; my strongest established fundamental-cell-biology option. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/)) |

I discount for a plausible Chemistry rather than Medicine award. ([gairdner.org](https://www.gairdner.org/resource-hub/2024-canada-gairdner-award-winners-announced)) |

The weak same-year Lasker base rate prevents an excessive increase. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/orexin-a-brain-peptide-that-maintains-wakefulness/?utm_source=openai)) |

I regard the signaling-plus-organoid framing as less straightforward than some competing discoveries. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/2/L29)) |

Its limited applicability as a general obesity treatment makes the clinical case less compelling than GLP-1's, without diminishing its physiological importance. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/leptin-a-hormone-that-regulates-appetite-and-body-weight/)) |

It remains distinct from computational structure prediction and competes closely with UPR. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/)) |

([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/breast-cancer-genetics-and-human-rights/)) |

A multiplier of 1.00 means **no net fresh-evidence adjustment**, not that the discovery has become unimportant. I also avoid an automatic bonus for being overdue: an old prize establishes maturity but does not reveal when Nobel recognition will occur.

## 4. Calculation and uncertainty adjustment

The baseline probabilities sum to 1. I calculated:

**w_i = b_i × m_i**

**q_i = w_i / Σw_i**

For the table above, **Σw_i = 1.21075**. The normalized evidence-weighted distribution gives GLP-1 0.228577328, orexin 0.082593434, and Other 0.258104481 before the final uncertainty adjustment.

To reduce confidence in my particular ranking and shortlist coverage, I mix this distribution with a deliberately more diffuse model:

- **r_Other = 0.40**;
- **r_i = 0.05** for each of the twelve listed discoveries;
- **p_i = 0.90 × q_i + 0.10 × r_i**.

The diffuse component sums to 1 because 0.40 + 12 × 0.05 = 1. Its purpose is to hedge against omitted committee priorities and mistaken relative rankings. The 10% mixture weight and 40% Other allocation are explicit modeling judgments, not measured frequencies.

For example:

**p_GLP-1 = 0.90 × (0.205 × 1.35 / 1.21075) + 0.10 × 0.05 = 0.210719595**.

**p_Other = 0.90 × (0.250 × 1.25 / 1.21075) + 0.10 × 0.40 = 0.272294033**.

I performed the normalization, mixture, and sum checks in Python. The reported probabilities, rounded to nine decimal places, sum to **1.000000000**. Those decimals preserve computational reproducibility; they do not imply that secret committee behavior can be estimated to nine-decimal accuracy.

## 5. Sensitivity, data quality, and remaining uncertainty

I tested **36 parameter combinations**, holding the baseline, other multipliers, and uncertainty mixture fixed. The GLP-1 multiplier took values 1.00, 1.20, 1.35, and 1.50; orexin took 1.50, 2.50, and 3.50; Other took 1.00, 1.25, and 1.50. Across those combinations, final probabilities ranged approximately from **15.4–24.8% for GLP-1**, **4.8–11.8% for orexin**, and **22.5–33.1% for Other**. These are model-sensitivity ranges, not statistical confidence intervals, and do not exhaust possible unknowns.

For historical numbers, the coverage window is **2000–2025**, with the current official-record vintage checked at the forecast cutoff. The Lasker statistic has **N = 25 award cycles**, not 26, because 2020 was cancelled. For contemporary evidence, I used publication or approval dates—not page footers—to establish availability before the cutoff. Older award records are identified by award year where a reliable original publication timestamp was not available.

Two freshness checks mattered. First, part of Lasker's 2026 essay still described the orexin agonist as late-stage development; the dated FDA approval establishes the newer status. Second, Gairdner's 2026 announcement has a March 31, 2026 page date but a 2025 year in its body dateline. I treated the latter as an apparent date inconsistency, not evidence that its 2026 awards occurred in 2025. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/2026-winners/?utm_source=openai))

The biggest unresolved variables are which discoveries received favorable confidential evaluations, how the Assembly handles competing attribution claims, and how broadly the official motivation is phrased. The short remaining horizon does not remove those uncertainties. **My conclusion is therefore a modest GLP-1 lead among individual discoveries, a substantial Other probability, and no listed discovery close to a majority probability.**

write_up:
## TL;DR
My forecast puts Other first at 30%, with GLP-1 the leading listed discovery at 23% ([calculation below](#evidence)). Orexin ranks second among listed discoveries at 13% ([calculation below](#evidence)). The main takeaway is to preserve substantial probability for discoveries outside the supplied list, rather than treat this as a two-candidate race ([omitted-discovery evidence](#evidence)).

## Context
This forecasts the official discovery motivation from the stipulated October 1, 2026 information cutoff. The Medicine announcement is scheduled for October 5, 2026, at 11:30 CEST at the earliest, or 09:30 UTC; the announcement remains a future event ([official schedule](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates/)).

I apply the client's discovery-level matching rule. Different laureates do not invalidate a matching discovery, and a listed scientist winning for different work does not make their option win. A divided award follows the supplied larger-share rule, then the first-mentioned-discovery tie-breaker. Historical discoveries and earlier awards are evidence, not prior resolutions.

## Evidence
The historical backbone argues against concentrating probability on a public favorite. Across the full completed 2000–2025 Medicine record, my tally finds 26 awards: 14 shared by three people, nine by two, and three awarded to one. Collaborative work is routinely compressed into a small recipient set. Attribution matters, but a discovery with more contributors than available places is not automatically excluded ([official Nobel record](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/all/)).

A discovery-level audit gives a stronger warning about award timing. The reference class contains 46 Basic or Clinical Lasker category-year awards from 2000–2023, excluding the cancelled 2020 awards, with each cohort observed through its complete same-year-to-two-years-later Medicine Nobel window ending no later than 2025. Using retrospective official records available at the cutoff, only one matched in the same year and two within that window: descriptive frequencies of 2% and 4%, respectively. These are proportions of award categories, not individual scientists or candidate-specific winning probabilities ([Basic archive](https://laskerfoundation.org/award/basic/), [Clinical archive](https://laskerfoundation.org/award/clinical/), [2020 cancellation](https://laskerfoundation.org/the-2020-lasker-awards/), [Nobel outcomes](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/all/)).

The same-year case is the 2013 Lasker for regulated neurotransmitter release and Nobel for vesicle-traffic machinery—a related-discovery match, not identical motivations. The other immediate-window case is the 2021 Clinical Lasker for modified mRNA followed by the 2023 Medicine Nobel. This small, classification-sensitive sample supports treating a new Lasker as evidence of scientific standing, not an October countdown clock ([2013 Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/regulated-neurotransmitter-release/), [2013 Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2013/press-release/), [2021 Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/2021-winners/), [2023 Nobel](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2023/press-release/)).

GLP-1 has the strongest listed combination of fundamental physiology and established therapeutic impact. The 2024 Clinical Lasker recognized Habener, Mojsov, and Knudsen for the discovery-to-obesity-treatment chain. The April 5, 2025 Breakthrough announcement recognized five contributors. On September 17, 2026, Clarivate selected Drucker, Holst, and Mojsov for GLP-1 identification, characterization, and biological activity. I read these differing citations as broad scientific validation, while counting their overlapping evidence only once—not as independent votes from the Nobel Assembly ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/), [Breakthrough announcement](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/91), [Clarivate announcement](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/)).

Orexin has the clearest fresh clinical milestone. On August 5, 2026, FDA approved oveporexton, which activates the receptor normally stimulated by orexin and addresses the deficient signaling underlying narcolepsy type 1. The September 9, 2026 Basic Lasker then recognized Mignot and Yanagisawa for orexin's wakefulness function and its deficiency in narcolepsy. That is a compact physiology, disease-mechanism, and treatment narrative. It makes orexin a strong contender, but the historical timing evidence does not justify making it the favorite solely because the Lasker is new ([FDA announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms), [Lasker release](https://laskerfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2026-press-release2.pdf)).

Other contains identifiable competition, not just unexplained uncertainty. Optical coherence tomography has both the 2023 Clinical Lasker and September 2026 Clarivate recognition. TOR-mediated growth regulation and cGAS DNA sensing have mature fundamental-discovery cases. Cystic-fibrosis combination therapy, retinal gene replacement, and fetal-hemoglobin regulation add credible clinical alternatives. These examples justify a substantial aggregate allocation without implying that any single omitted discovery outranks GLP-1 ([OCT](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/optical-coherence-tomography/), [Clarivate](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/), [TOR](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/nutrient-activated-tor-proteins-that-regulate-cell-growth/), [cGAS](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/), [cystic fibrosis](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/combined-triple-drug-therapy-for-cystic-fibrosis/), [April 18, 2026 Breakthrough announcement](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/98)).

The remaining listed discoveries retain meaningful probability. Their relative positions reflect scientific framing, attribution, and category competition—not a requirement for a marketed treatment.

| Discovery | Evidence and forecast judgment |
|---|---|
| Chaperone-mediated folding | A compact fundamental-discovery case, backed by the 2011 Lasker. Hartl's September 18, 2026 Keio recognition supplies modest additional corroboration ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/), [Keio](https://www.keio.ac.jp/en/press-release/20260918-press-01/)). |
| Unfolded protein response | The 2014 Lasker recognizes a distinct cellular stress-response mechanism with relatively clear attribution ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/)). |

| Next-generation sequencing | The May 13, 2026 Princess of Asturias citation confirms its broad biomedical importance. | Anti-TNF | A mature, clinically transformative case. Its long wait is not evidence of disqualification ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/anti-tnf-for-treating-rheumatoid-arthritis/)). |

The 2024 Chemistry Nobel concerned computational protein design and structure prediction. It did not recognize cellular chaperone machinery or the unfolded protein response, so I do not exclude either protein-related option as already awarded ([official motivation](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/)).

For the numerical construction, I averaged the supplied distributions equally, then made limited relative-weight corrections. I increased GLP-1 and Other by 10%, CAR-T by 8%, and chaperones by 4%; reduced orexin by 15%; and left other weights unchanged. These are relative-weight changes, not percentage-point changes. They reflect the discovery-matching correction, omitted competition, verified Tang and Keio signals, and restraint on immediate Lasker timing. Each pooled probability was multiplied by its adjustment and divided by the total adjusted weight. The adjustments are judgmental, not measured likelihood ratios. Six-decimal largest-remainder rounding preserves a total probability of one; the digits preserve arithmetic, not predictive certainty. No market prices enter the estimate.

## What's non-obvious
The recipient roster is less constraining than it first appears. Habener died on December 28, 2025, which ends his eligibility for a new Nobel, not GLP-1's eligibility as a discovery. The three-person limit still creates a credit-allocation problem, but Clarivate's living Drucker–Holst–Mojsov trio demonstrates a coherent alternative. I therefore reject both extremes: treating attribution as irrelevant, and treating a mismatched roster as a discovery-level veto ([NAS record](https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/joel-f-habener-jpqij9/), [Nobel statutes](https://www.nobelprize.org/statutes-of-the-nobel-foundation/), [Clarivate citation](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/)).

A current-year award webpage can also create false momentum. Brangwynne and Hyman appear in Breakthrough's 2026 ceremony material, but their phase-separation prize was awarded in 2023; their ceremony appearance was delayed by the pandemic. I retain phase separation within Other, but do not give it an invented new-prize boost ([Foundation's ceremony account](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/99)).

## Uncertainties
The decisive missing evidence is the Assembly's private discovery ranking and attribution analysis. Nomination and evaluation material remains confidential for 50 years, so I cannot verify a current shortlist or committee preference. Public awards establish scientific standing; they do not reveal the confidential decision. Precise motivation also leaves matching risk for broad packages such as cellular immunotherapy or combined protein-quality-control work ([Nobel annual review](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2025/04/annual-review-2024.pdf), [Tang's broader motivation](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097)).

The largest numerical uncertainty is shortlist coverage, followed by the weight placed on recent recognition. Removing the orexin discount raises its estimate from 13% to 15%; removing the omitted-field uplift reduces Other from 30% to 28% ([forecast construction](#evidence)). Those are narrow model-sensitivity tests, not confidence intervals. Uncertainty about the starting judgments is wider, and the short remaining horizon does not remove uncertainty about a private selection.

The prize is awarded for a discovery, not simply for current popularity or commercial success. Nobel rules allow no more than three recipients and generally prohibit posthumous awards. I first formed an independent estimate without consulting prediction markets. I assigned **25.5% to Other**, reflecting the large universe of Nobel-caliber work omitted from the options, and distributed the remaining 74.5% using six considerations:

1. Scientific importance and demonstrated durability.

4. Fit with Physiology or Medicine rather than Chemistry.
5. Precursor-prize consensus and maturity.
6. Decision-relevant 2026 weak signals, with a penalty for signals announced after the Nobel nomination deadline because they cannot prove nomination or causally create eligibility.

Late awards are nevertheless informative because independent expert committees may be converging on the same mature discovery. After fixing the independent ranking, I searched for a matching prediction market but did not find a usable market distribution, so no market-based adjustment was made.

GLP-1 combines an established physiological discovery with unusually clear therapeutic consequences. The official 2024 Clinical Lasker account describes identification of the active hormone and the engineering of longer-lasting medicines for obesity. Its foundational work dates to the 1980s, so the case is not dependent on rewarding a recent commercial fashion before its underlying science has matured. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/))

Recognition has continued across multiple award cycles. The April 5, 2025 Breakthrough announcement honored Drucker, Habener, Holst, Knudsen, and Mojsov for the discovery-to-therapy sequence. Mojsov is the **2026 King Faisal Medicine laureate**, specifically for active GLP-1 and its therapeutic implications. Clarivate’s **September 17, 2026** announcement additionally recognized Drucker, Holst, and Mojsov. I treat these as correlated validation signals, not three independent confirmations of Nobel selection; Clarivate itself says its program is not intended to predict recipients in a particular year. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/91))

The main counterweight is attribution. Different prestigious awards choose different subsets of contributors, and Breakthrough recognized five people. **Joel Habener died on December 28, 2025**, according to the National Academy of Sciences, so he is not normally eligible for a 2026 Nobel. This does not eliminate the discovery option, but choosing among the remaining major contributors is still difficult. I regard this as a moderate obstacle—not a large exact-roster penalty, since the question expressly matches by discovery. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/91))

### Orexin — strongest fresh competing signal

The **2026 Basic Lasker**, announced September 9, recognizes Mignot and Yanagisawa for orexin’s role in wakefulness and orexin deficiency in narcolepsy. I checked the award against Stanford’s dated institutional report before treating it as current evidence. The Lasker account also describes de Lecea’s independent identification of the same peptides under the name hypocretins; a Nobel motivation using that terminology would still match the orexin discovery. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/orexin-a-brain-peptide-that-maintains-wakefulness/))

The clinical-readiness case strengthened when the FDA approved **Orzeyful/oveporexton on August 5, 2026**, targeting the deficient orexin signaling underlying narcolepsy type 1. This links a fundamental sleep-regulation discovery to a mechanism-directed treatment. It raises orexin substantially above a generic longstanding contender, although the historical same-year Lasker evidence counsels against making it the overwhelming favorite. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms))

### Unfolded protein response versus chaperone-mediated folding

The UPR has a particularly clean discovery package: Mori and Walter elucidated an ER stress-sensing and corrective signaling system, with pivotal work in 1993. Their **2014 Basic Lasker** recognizes that mechanism. The compact attribution and fundamental cellular-homeostasis significance make it my strongest listed alternative in basic cell biology after accounting for orexin’s fresh evidence. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/))

Hartl and Horwich’s chaperone work is comparably foundational: the pivotal 1989 experiments established cellular machinery assisting protein folding, and their **2011 Basic Lasker** recognized the folding apparatus. Its clean two-person core is a significant advantage. I nevertheless place it slightly below UPR for this particular Medicine award. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/))

The **October 9, 2024 Chemistry motivation** concerned computational protein design and protein structure prediction. Those are not the cellular folding machinery or ER stress signaling. Accordingly, I do not consider either listed discovery already rewarded. My modest discount to chaperones reflects possible thematic adjacency and category competition, not scientific duplication; UPR has a more clearly distinct stress-signaling narrative. The focused scientific review led me to transfer four percentage points within the fundamental-mechanism scenario from chaperones to UPR, increasing UPR’s final forecast by 1.8 percentage points and reducing chaperones by the same amount. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2024/press-release/b/?utm_source=openai))

### CAR-T

CAR-T has strong treatment impact and fresh recognition. The **June 16, 2026 Tang Prize** jointly honored Rosenberg, Sadelain, and June for TIL and CAR-T cellular immunotherapy. This strengthens the case and demonstrates that another major award could assemble a three-person recognition package. However, Tang’s discovery is broader than CAR-T alone: a Nobel focused primarily on TIL rather than CAR-T could resolve Other under the supplied rules. I therefore avoid transferring the full cellular-immunotherapy case into this option. ([tang-prize.org](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097))

### Other listed options

- **Optogenetics:** Its 2021 Basic Lasker confirms a mature, transformative neuroscience method. It receives substantial probability in the enabling-method scenario, but less in a scenario emphasizing established clinical interventions. This is a distinction in demonstrated application, not a claim that the Nobel requires a marketed treatment. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/light-sensitive-microbial-proteins-optogenetics/))
- **PCSK9:** A strong human-genetics-to-treatment story, with a fresh clinical milestone: FDA approval of the first oral PCSK9 inhibitor, enlicitide/Lipfendra, on **July 17, 2026**. I give this a modest readiness boost, while judging the field less likely than GLP-1 to dominate a therapeutics-oriented selection. ([fda.gov](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-oral-pcsk9-inhibitor-lower-ldl-cholesterol-adults-high-cholesterol?trk=public_post_comment-text))
- **Next-generation sequencing:** The 2024 Gairdner recognition of Balasubramanian, Klenerman, and Mayer supports its broad biomedical importance. Its lower Medicine probability reflects uncertainty about category placement, not doubts about significance or a requirement that Mayer appear in the option. ([gairdner.org](https://www.gairdner.org/resource-hub/2024-gairdner-international-symposium))
- **Wnt/organoids:** Clevers’ work has established stem-cell, cancer-research, and organoid applications. I consider it credible, but the listed label combines a signaling discovery with a related cultivation technology. A narrowly framed official motivation could introduce matching uncertainty. ([epo.org](https://www.epo.org/en/news-events/european-inventor-award/meet-the-finalists/hans-clevers))
- **Leptin:** The 2010 Basic Lasker validates a fundamental discovery about hormonal regulation of body weight. Its conceptual case is strong; its therapeutic breadth is less compelling than GLP-1’s, so it receives more weight in the fundamental scenario than the clinical one. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/leptin-a-hormone-that-regulates-appetite-and-body-weight/))
- **Anti-TNF:** The 2003 Clinical Lasker establishes a major therapeutic paradigm in autoimmune disease. Its low forecast is not a judgment that it is unworthy or too old; it reflects competition from numerous comparable discoveries and limited fresh discriminating evidence in the sources reviewed. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/anti-tnf-for-treating-rheumatoid-arthritis/))
- **BRCA susceptibility genes:** King’s 2018 Shaw recognition supports the importance of hereditary breast-cancer genetics. I retain a nontrivial chance, but broader recognition spanning mapping, cloning, and multiple susceptibility genes requires a less straightforward discovery-and-credit package than UPR or orexin. ([newsroom.uw.edu](https://newsroom.uw.edu/blog/mary-claire-king-receive-shaw-prize-china/))

## 4. Why Other deserves substantial probability

The shortlist is strong but demonstrably incomplete. Especially consequential omissions include:

1. **cGAS-mediated DNA sensing**, recognized by the 2024 Basic Lasker. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/))
2. **Acute promyelocytic leukemia mechanisms and targeted combination therapy**, recognized by the Shaw Prize announcement of **May 27, 2026**. This is the award foundation’s own distributed announcement, not an independent journalist’s prediction. ([newswire.ca](https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/announcement-of-the-shaw-laureates-2026-811785529.html))
3. **Phase separation in cellular organization, the fetal-to-adult hemoglobin switch, and retinal gene-replacement therapy**, all represented in the official 2026 Breakthrough laureate list. ([breakthroughprize.org](https://breakthroughprize.org/laureates-2026))
4. **Optical coherence tomography and cystic-fibrosis combination therapy**, represented by the 2023 and 2025 Clinical Laskers respectively; the 2026 Clinical Lasker also recognizes hemophilia-A bispecific-antibody therapy. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/award/clinical/))

The 2026 Gairdner list supplies further omitted routes, including proteomics, cryo-electron tomography, and aggregation-directed therapy. I noticed that its March 31, 2026 page retains a 2025 dateline in one introductory sentence; I treat that as a date-copy inconsistency and do not derive a precise timing signal from it. ([gairdner.org](https://www.gairdner.org/resource-hub/2026-canada-gairdner-award-winners))

These omissions are not equally likely, and counting them equally would not produce a calibrated Other probability. Nevertheless, the review establishes that Other is a substantial competing pool rather than a token residual. My 31.65% allocation is toward the lower end of a roughly 30–40% shortlist-coverage judgment, because the supplied list captures unusually strong discoveries such as GLP-1, orexin, UPR, and CAR-T. That range is an elicited sensitivity assessment, not an observed historical frequency.

## 5. Reproducible numerical model

I use a three-scenario probability mixture to avoid committing entirely to one view of what the Assembly will emphasize:

- **Fundamental physiological/cellular mechanism: 45% weight.**
- **Transformative clinical intervention: 40% weight.**
- **Enabling research method or platform: 15% weight.**

These are subjective organizing scenarios, not verified committee agendas, mutually exclusive scientific classifications, or parameters fitted from 20 historical awards. The relatively high clinical weight reflects the strength of the current GLP-1, orexin, CAR-T, and PCSK9 evidence. The substantial fundamental weight reflects both the historical breadth of Medicine awards and the recent mechanism-oriented selections. I do not use a deterministic field-rotation rule.

The following inputs are **percent probabilities within each scenario**. Each column sums to 100:

| Resolving discovery | Fundamental | Clinical | Methods/platforms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GLP-1 | 8.0 | 40.0 | 5.0 |
| Optogenetics | 4.0 | 0.1 | 20.0 |
| CAR-T | 2.0 | 11.5 | 6.0 |
| Unfolded protein response | 16.0 | 0.5 | 2.5 |
| PCSK9 | 0.7 | 4.5 | 0.5 |
| Next-generation sequencing | 0.5 | 0.1 | 10.0 |
| Orexin | 15.0 | 10.0 | 8.0 |
| Wnt/organoids | 3.0 | 0.5 | 6.0 |
| Leptin | 3.5 | 1.5 | 0.5 |
| Anti-TNF | 0.1 | 2.5 | 0.5 |
| Chaperone-mediated folding | 11.0 | 0.8 | 2.5 |
| BRCA susceptibility genes | 1.2 | 2.5 | 0.5 |
| Other | 35.0 | 25.5 | 38.0 |

For every option i, I calculate **p(i) = 0.45 × fundamental(i) + 0.40 × clinical(i) + 0.15 × methods(i)**, converting the percentage inputs to probabilities. For example, GLP-1 is 0.45×0.08 + 0.40×0.40 + 0.15×0.05 = **0.20350**. Other is 0.45×0.35 + 0.40×0.255 + 0.15×0.38 = **0.31650**. Python calculations and a decimal-arithmetic check confirm that the 13 resulting probabilities sum to **1.00000**.

## 6. Uncertainty and sensitivity

The dominant uncertainty is the Assembly’s unobserved selection among many scientifically credible discoveries, not whether these accomplishments are important. Award signals are correlated, there is no public current shortlist, and exact official motivation can matter for broad or combined discovery packages.

The scenario weights materially affect the answer. Holding the table fixed, weights of **60% fundamental / 25% clinical / 15% methods** produce GLP-1 **15.55%**, UPR **10.10%**, and Other **33.075%**. Weights of **30% / 55% / 15%** produce GLP-1 **25.15%**, UPR **5.45%**, and Other **30.225%**. These are sensitivity calculations, not confidence bounds; changing the within-scenario judgments or omitted-candidate pool would widen the uncertainty further.

Thus the final digits represent arithmetic precision, not comparable evidential certainty. The robust conclusions are: **GLP-1 leads the individually listed discoveries; orexin merits a meaningful upward reassessment on current evidence; UPR slightly outranks chaperone folding for this Medicine award; and concentrating most probability on the supplied shortlist’s best-known names would understate the credible omitted field.**

## Context
The information cutoff is the client's October 1, 2026, 23:20 UTC. For divided prizes, I use the larger discovery share and then the first-mentioned discovery for equal shares. Attribution remains relevant to selection because Nobel prizes can name no more than three individuals, but the names printed in an option are not a resolution requirement ([Nobel rules](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/07/annual_review_13.pdf)).

The historical backbone is an audit of all 20 Medicine prize years from 2006 through 2025, using historical award records available at the cutoff.
