The three asterisked matches concern the second-listed, equal-share discovery. Applying this question's tie-break reduces the precursor overlap to 10 of 20 selected discoveries, or 50.0%. This distinction prevents a recipient-level statistic from being mistaken for a discovery-level base rate ([2008 announcement](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2008/press-release/), [2011 announcement](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2011/press-release/), [2015 announcement](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2015/press-release/)).

They establish that precursor recognition supports Nobel stature much more strongly than immediate timing ([Basic archive](https://laskerfoundation.org/award/basic/), [Clinical archive](https://laskerfoundation.org/award/clinical/), [Nobel records](https://api.nobelprize.org/2/nobelPrizes)).

GLP-1 has the strongest listed combination of mature biological discovery, demonstrated therapeutic impact, and recent recognition. Its program received the 2024 Lasker Clinical award and the 2025 Breakthrough Prize. On September 17, 2026, Clarivate recognized Drucker, Holst, and Mojsov for foundational GLP-1 biology. I read the latter as support for a discovery-centered Nobel framing, not merely recognition of successful drug development. The counterweight is attribution across several complementary contributions: the Breakthrough award recognized five scientists. That creates selection friction, not a discovery-matching failure ([Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/), [Breakthrough](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/91), [dated Clarivate announcement](https://ir.clarivate.com/news-events/press-releases/news-details/2026/Clarivate-Reveals-Citation-Laureates-2026-Recognizing-Transformative-Scientific-Breakthroughs/default.aspx)).

The FDA's August 5, 2026 approval of oveporexton supplies a targeted treatment that restores missing orexin signaling. This strengthens an already established case: Mignot and Yanagisawa had received the 2023 Breakthrough Prize. I elevate orexin without treating the latest award as a Nobel preview or counting these related signals as independent evidence ([dated Lasker release](https://laskerfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2026-press-release2.pdf), [FDA approval](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms), [earlier recognition](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/73)).

Their Lasker citations describe distinct cellular mechanisms with relatively tractable core attribution. Optogenetics has a strong enabling-method case; the historical award for gene-targeted mice shows that a research tool need not wait for a direct therapy. I therefore reject a categorical penalty against methods, while retaining uncertainty about contributor selection ([UPR](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/), [chaperones](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/), [optogenetics](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/light-sensitive-microbial-proteins-optogenetics/), [method precedent](https://api.nobelprize.org/2/nobelPrize/med/2007)).

CAR-T gains support from the February 11, 2026 BBVA award to June and Sadelain and the June 16, 2026 Tang award. The latter also recognizes tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy, so its entire evidential weight cannot be transferred to CAR-T. PCSK9 receives a smaller positive update from the FDA's July 17, 2026 announcement of the first oral inhibitor; that validates the target without establishing Nobel priority ([BBVA](https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/noticias/18th-edition-frontiers-of-knowledge-award-biology-biomedicine-carl-june-michel-sadelain/), [Tang](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097), [FDA](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-oral-pcsk9-inhibitor-lower-ldl-cholesterol-adults-high-cholesterol)).

Wnt/organoids, leptin, anti-TNF, and inherited breast/ovarian cancer susceptibility retain credible cases, but share probability with a large pool of comparable achievements. Their lower allocations are relative judgments, not deductions from missing headlines or claims that older discoveries are ineligible. The strongest additional research finding is acute promyelocytic leukemia: its molecular basis and targeted combination therapy received the 2026 Shaw Prize, following the same program's 2018 Sjöberg recognition. Further omissions include integrins, cell-free fetal DNA and prenatal testing, cGAS DNA sensing, and TOR-dependent growth control—all with major Lasker recognition. Clarivate's current Medicine selections also include OCT and immune adhesion receptors, both outside this shortlist ([APL announcement, May 27, 2026](https://www.academie-sciences.fr/en/anne-dejean-hugues-de-and-zhu-chen-receive-shaw-prize), [earlier APL recognition](https://www.pasteur.fr/en/whats-new/press-area/press-releases-and-press-kits/anne-dejean-assemat-receives-sjoberg-prize-2018), [integrins](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/integrins-mediators-of-cell-matrix-cell-adhesion/), [prenatal DNA](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/noninvasive-prenatal-testing-using-fetal-dna/), [cGAS](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/), [TOR](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/nutrient-activated-tor-proteins-that-regulate-cell-growth/), [Clarivate selections](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/)).

The numerical allocation balances broad-field, fundamental-discovery, translation, and enabling-method views. After auditing the evidence, I retain more omitted-field mass, strengthen CAR-T modestly, and reduce Medicine-specific sequencing probability. The final distribution reserves 35.0% for Other; conditional on a listed discovery winning, GLP-1 receives 28% and orexin 17%. These are judgmental weights, not fitted likelihood ratios. Normalization makes the outcomes mutually exclusive and exhaustive.

## What's non-obvious
**Attribution risk is not resolution risk.** A GLP-1 prize with a different trio still matches the option, so reproducing another award's recipients is unnecessary. The opposite distinction matters too: a Nobel centered on TIL therapy would not automatically count as CAR-T merely because overlapping scientists won it. Likewise, fetal-DNA discovery is distinct from developing sequencing methods ([GLP-1 recognition](https://clarivate.com/citation-laureates/physiology-medicine/), [TIL versus CAR-T](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097), [fetal-DNA discovery](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/noninvasive-prenatal-testing-using-fetal-dna/)).

The public-award narrative also hides a denominator problem. Frequent Lasker recognition among Nobel winners does not imply a high next-Nobel probability for a new Lasker winner. Nor does a low same-year conversion rate cap orexin's chance: the current candidate is not a randomly selected historical award entry. I use precursor awards to assess stature and maturity, then assess timing separately against the competing field ([historical award pool](https://laskerfoundation.org/award/basic/), [Nobel record](https://api.nobelprize.org/2/nobelPrizes)).

## Uncertainties
The largest missing information is the committee's assessment of candidates and credit allocation. Nomination and evaluation material remains confidential for 50 years. A prospectively assembled candidate-pool backtest would improve calibration; retrospective overlaps alone cannot supply reliable annual discovery-level probabilities. I verified the Wolf designations on official individual profiles, but not a separately dated announcement, so their timing receives less weight than the dated Lasker, FDA, and Clarivate evidence ([confidentiality rules](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/07/annual_review_13.pdf), [Wolf taste profile](https://wolffund.org.il/charles-s-zuker/), [Wolf sequencing profile](https://wolffund.org.il/shankar-balasubramanian/)).

My main sensitivity test changes Other from 28% to 45.0% while preserving the relative weights of listed discoveries. GLP-1 then ranges from 15% to 20%, and orexin from 10% to 12%. These are assumption-sensitivity ranges, not statistical confidence intervals. The submitted decimal places preserve the normalized calculation; they do not imply millionth-level forecasting accuracy.

## 1. Interpretation and research approach

I forecast the **discovery that will resolve the question**, not the exact combination of laureates. Consequently, a GLP-1 award involving Daniel Drucker or Joel Habener would still count for the GLP-1 option; an optogenetics award with a different recipient combination would still count for optogenetics. I also apply the question's larger-share and first-mentioned tie rules. The probabilities are not probabilities that a discovery will merely appear somewhere in a divided award.

The distinction between discovery and recipients is important. Nobel rules limit a prize to three individuals, so complicated attribution can make selection harder, but a mismatch between the names in an option and another award's recipients is **not itself a reason to reject that option**. The three-person limit is documented by NobelPrize.org. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/facts-on-the-nobel-prize-in-physiology-or-medicine/?utm_source=openai))

I used official Nobel records through the Nobel-data API, primary award citations from Lasker, Breakthrough, and Gairdner, FDA announcements, Clarivate's original recognition announcement, and institutional scientific sources. I also searched contemporary news through Perigon and commissioned an independent award-history research report. The report was useful for challenging my ranking, particularly on orexin, but its numerical recommendations were not mechanically incorporated. I did not consult prediction-market prices, betting odds, or public probability aggregates.

My decision-relevant research threads were:

1. **Have fresh 2026 recognitions changed the ranking?** Yes: orexin received the 2026 Lasker Basic award, while GLP-1 received fresh Clarivate recognition.
2. **Has a candidate recently crossed from biological discovery into demonstrated treatment?** Yes: the August 2026 FDA announcement for an orexin agonist materially strengthened orexin's translational case; a July FDA announcement also strengthened PCSK9's continuing clinical relevance.
3. **Could a Nobel-worthy achievement be awarded in Chemistry instead of Medicine?** This is a material concern for sequencing and, to a lesser degree, chaperone-assisted folding.
4. **Does the supplied shortlist omit serious competitors?** Yes. Several recent major-award discoveries fall under Other.

## 2. Historical reference class and its limitations

I retrieved **16 annual Medicine prizes, covering 2010–2025 inclusive**, with announcement dates running from October 4, 2010 through October 6, 2025. The unit is one prize-year, not one laureate. These are retrospective official records available at the forecast cutoff, rather than a reconstructed contemporaneous candidate database. NobelPrize.org independently supplies the historical motivations. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/?utm_source=openai))

Using a deliberately narrow coding rule—whether the motivation explicitly centers on developing treatment or enabling a therapeutic intervention—I classify **2010, 2015, 2018, and 2023** as clearly therapeutic: IVF, antiparasitic therapies, checkpoint cancer therapy, and modified-mRNA vaccines. That gives **4/16 = 25%**. This is my classification, not an official Nobel statistic, and it does not imply that the remaining prizes lacked clinical importance. Its forecasting implication is modest: an exceptionally successful medicine does not automatically outrank fundamental physiology or cell biology. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/all/?utm_source=openai))

Recent awards also illustrate breadth: the 2022 prize concerned ancient genomes and human evolution, 2024 concerned microRNA, and 2025 concerned peripheral immune tolerance. Thus, focusing exclusively on prominent treatments would overlook plausible selection styles. I do not impose a rule against consecutive immunology awards merely because immune tolerance won in 2025. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/?utm_source=openai))

I did **not** calculate a Lasker-to-Nobel conversion probability. A defensible estimate would require a complete historical candidate pool, announcement-date alignment, category routing, and treatment of right-censored researchers. Simply counting famous scientists who eventually won both prizes would create substantial selection bias. Moreover, Nobel nomination and evaluation records remain confidential for 50 years, so public recognition is evidence of scientific standing—not access to the committee's current shortlist. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2025/04/annual-review-2024.pdf?utm_source=openai))

## 5. Numerical construction: reproducible judgmental model

- **F: fundamental physiological/cellular discovery**, weight **0.50**.
- **T: discovery-to-treatment translation**, weight **0.35**.
- **M: enabling methods/platforms**, weight **0.15**.

These weights are subjective. The historical sample motivates retaining substantial fundamental-discovery weight, while current GLP-1 and orexin evidence motivates meaningful translation weight. The models are alternative perspectives, not official mutually exclusive Nobel categories.

## 6. Reproducible numerical construction

I combined two judgmental models. They are not independently fitted statistical models; the purpose of combining them is to reduce reliance on one organizing assumption.

### Model A: historical thematic mixture

Starting with the historical counts 9, 8, and 3, I added **four smoothing pseudo-counts to each group**. The resulting thematic weights are:

- Molecular/cellular/genetic/evolutionary: **13/32 = 0.40625**.
- Disease/immunology/treatment: **12/32 = 0.375**.
- Neural/systems physiology: **7/32 = 0.21875**.

The smoothing prevents the small historical sample from making the physiology weight excessively low. Within each group, I assigned the following conditional probabilities based on the evidence above:

- Molecular/cellular: UPR 0.20; chaperone folding 0.17; sequencing 0.065; Wnt 0.075; Other 0.49.
- Disease/treatment: GLP-1 0.48; CAR-T 0.18; PCSK9 0.10; anti-TNF 0.055; cancer susceptibility genes 0.065; Other 0.12.
- Neural/physiology: optogenetics 0.30; orexin 0.40; leptin 0.11; Other 0.19.

Each conditional group sums to one. Multiplying by the group weights and adding contributions produces Model A below.

### Model B: discovery-level relative weights

I independently assigned relative weights reflecting significance, maturity, recognition, category fit, and omitted competition. These are **subjective cardinal weights**, not measured citation counts or estimated likelihood ratios. Their sum is **36.50**; Model B probability is each weight divided by 36.50.

During final evidence review, I applied small relative-weight refinements: **1.15 for CAR-T**, reflecting the verified 2026 Tang recognition while discounting its broader TIL component; **1.10 for orexin**, reflecting the strength of the verified mechanism-restoring FDA approval and controlled validation; and **1.00 for every other outcome**. ## 3. Historical calibration: precursor recognition helps, but is not an annual oracle

A manual cross-check of the **20 annual Medicine Nobels from 2006 through 2025** found a verified earlier Basic or Clinical Lasker recipient among the Nobel laureates in **13 award years: 65%**. The matched years were 2007, 2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2015, 2018, 2019, 2020, 2023, and 2024. Public Service and Special Achievement Laskers were excluded. Nobel records were checked against Foundation recipient pages; indexed primary material was used where direct access was limited. This is a manual verified-intersection audit, not an exhaustive machine-readable roster match. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/laureates/?utm_source=openai))

Only **one of those 20 Nobel award years** had a same-calendar-year Basic/Clinical Lasker match: Thomas Südhof in 2013. For the 13 matched years, defining the annual lag as Nobel year minus the earliest qualifying Lasker year among that year's laureates gives: **6, 22, 3, 9, 4, 3, 11, 4, 3, 3, 20, 2, 16 years**. The median is **4 years**. These are my calculations from the award-year records, with information vintage limited to the forecast cutoff. ([nobelprize.org](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/laureates/?utm_source=openai))

Three cautions prevent misuse of these figures. First, 65% measures precursor overlap **among Nobel winners**, not the probability that a Lasker winner receives the next Nobel. Second, the calculation counts any laureate in a year, rather than only the discovery selected by this question's split-prize rule. Third, many unawarded discoveries remain in a decades-deep queue. My resulting judgment is that a Lasker is substantial evidence of eligibility and stature, but a September Lasker should not be interpreted as knowledge of October's selection.

The six Medicine Nobels from 2020–2025 also illustrate the breadth of the outcome space: hepatitis C, temperature/touch receptors, extinct-hominin genomics, modified-nucleoside mRNA vaccines, microRNA, and peripheral immune tolerance. The **2010 Lasker Basic award** to Coleman and Friedman recognized leptin and hormonal regulation of appetite and body weight. It is an established physiological breakthrough. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/leptin-a-hormone-that-regulates-appetite-and-body-weight/))

Within the metabolic-discovery competition, however, I judge GLP-1's combined current recognition and therapeutic story more compelling for 2026. This is a relative ranking, not a suggestion that a GLP-1 prize would already recognize leptin or make leptin ineligible.

### TNF as a therapeutic target

The **2003 Lasker Clinical award** to Feldmann and Maini recognized anti-TNF therapy for rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases. Its mature clinical impact and identifiable central contribution are positives. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/anti-tnf-for-treating-rheumatoid-arthritis/))

I give it a smaller share because the field has remained in the candidate queue for a long period without a comparably strong fresh signal retrieved here. I treat that absence cautiously: it is not evidence about confidential nominations or committee evaluations.

### Inherited breast/ovarian cancer susceptibility genes

King's **2014 Lasker Special Achievement award** recognized, among other work, identifying the BRCA1 locus associated with hereditary breast cancer. It is important to distinguish this from a Basic or Clinical Lasker; it was therefore excluded from the historical precursor calculation above. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/breast-cancer-genetics-and-human-rights/))

The genetics and preventive-medicine case remains credible. My lower allocation reflects competition and the possibility of alternative discovery framings across linkage identification, gene isolation, and the broader inherited-susceptibility story—not a requirement that King, Skolnick, and Stratton all be selected.

## 5. Why Other receives substantial probability

Other contains several contenders with recognition comparable to the named options:

- **Integrins/cell adhesion:** Hynes, Ruoslahti, and Springer received the **2022 Lasker Basic award**. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/integrins-mediators-of-cell-matrix-cell-adhesion/))
- **Optical coherence tomography:** Fujimoto, Huang, and Swanson received the **2023 Lasker Clinical award**. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/optical-coherence-tomography/))
- **cGAS DNA sensing:** Chen received the **2024 Lasker Basic award**. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/))
- **Low-complexity domains and cystic-fibrosis triple-drug therapy:** these were the **2025 Lasker Basic and Clinical discoveries**, announced September 11, 2025. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/2025-lasker-award-press-release-f.pdf))

The new evidence also supports omitted fields. Of Clarivate's **three 2026 Medicine discovery clusters**, only GLP-1 is listed here; OCT and immune-cell adhesion receptors are omitted. This is a count of recognized discovery clusters, **N=3**, not a forecast hit rate. ([ir.clarivate.com](https://ir.clarivate.com/news-events/press-releases/news-details/2026/Clarivate-Reveals-Citation-Laureates-2026-Recognizing-Transformative-Scientific-Breakthroughs/default.aspx))

Additional current recognition includes local protein translation in neurons in the **June 10, 2026 Kavli announcement**, and acute promyelocytic leukemia biology and targeted treatment in the **May 27, 2026 Shaw announcement**. Both fall outside the listed discovery categories. ([kavliprize.org](https://www.kavliprize.org/2026-kavli-prize-laureates-announced))

I therefore resist allocating nearly all probability among the familiar listed candidates. Other also includes less-publicized discoveries and unforeseen official-motivation framings. Its size reflects an aggregated field of competitors, not a belief that any one omitted discovery is more likely than GLP-1.

## 6. Numerical construction

I used a transparent **judgmental relative-support model**, rather than claiming that public awards identify empirical annual win probabilities. The baseline incorporates established track records, scientific maturity, Medicine fit, attribution feasibility, and the breadth of the omitted pool. I then apply restrained 2026 evidence-bundle multipliers. They are **not fitted likelihood ratios**.

| Discovery | Baseline probability | 2026 support multiplier |
|---|---:|---:|
| GLP-1 | 0.145 | 1.65 |
| Optogenetics | 0.055 | 1.00 |
| CAR-T | 0.055 | 1.00 |
| Unfolded protein response | 0.060 | 1.00 |
| PCSK9 | 0.040 | 1.00 |
| Next-generation sequencing | 0.030 | 1.25 |
| Orexin | 0.055 | 3.00 |
| Wnt/organoids | 0.025 | 1.00 |
| Leptin | 0.020 | 1.00 |
| TNF | 0.018 | 1.00 |
| Chaperone-mediated folding | 0.075 | 1.00 |
| Breast/ovarian susceptibility genes | 0.022 | 1.00 |
| Other | 0.400 | 1.18 |

The baseline sums to 1. The GLP-1 multiplier reflects fresh Clarivate recognition; orexin's larger multiplier reflects the combined Lasker and FDA developments; sequencing receives a smaller current-recognition update; and Other receives an update for fresh omitted-field recognition. Importantly, I use **one multiplier per evidence bundle** rather than multiplying correlated award signals as if they were independent observations.

For each category i, the calculation is:

**P(i) = baseline(i) × multiplier(i) / sum of all baseline × multiplier products.**

The denominator is **1.28375**. For example, GLP-1 is **0.145 × 1.65 / 1.28375 = 0.1863680623...**; orexin is **0.055 × 3 / 1.28375 = 0.1285296981...**. Python was used to normalize every category and verify the total. The output is rounded to eight decimal places, with a one-in-one-hundred-million rounding adjustment to Other so the reported probabilities sum exactly to 1.

## 7. Sensitivity and remaining uncertainty

The largest modeling uncertainty is the breadth of the omitted pool. Holding the relative distribution within the named options and all multipliers fixed, changing the baseline Other allocation from **30% to 50%** changes the final Other probability from **27.21% to 46.59%**. Under the same exercise, GLP-1 ranges from **21.45% to 15.74%**, and orexin from **14.80% to 10.86%**. These are model-sensitivity results, not statistically estimated confidence intervals.

Fresh-signal strength is another uncertainty. A weaker update set—GLP-1 1.35, orexin 1.8, sequencing 1.10, Other 1.05—produces approximately **17.51% GLP-1, 8.86% orexin, and 37.58% Other**. A stronger set—2.0, 3.8, 1.4, and 1.3 respectively—produces approximately **20.27%, 14.61%, and 36.34%**. This shows why orexin deserves a meaningful upgrade without treating its current-year recognition as decisive.

The final estimate balances demonstrated biomedical importance against confidential selection, correlated prestige signals, category competition, attribution constraints, and omitted discoveries. **The eight decimal places express numerical reproducibility, not eight-decimal epistemic certainty.** GLP-1 leads the named discoveries, but neither it nor any other individual listed discovery warrants a majority probability on the public evidence available at the cutoff.

## TL;DR
My forecast puts GLP-1 first among the listed discoveries at 17%, followed by orexin at 11%. Other is the largest resolution category at 32.0%, reflecting the strength of discoveries missing from the list. Recent scientific prizes establish importance, not the Nobel Assembly’s choice ([selection process](https://www.nobelprize.org/nomination)).

## Context
The forecast cutoff is October 1, 2026, at 22:51 UTC. The Medicine announcement is scheduled for October 5, 2026, at 11:30 CEST at the earliest, equivalent to 09:30 UTC ([official schedule](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/about/prize-announcement-dates/)). Earlier discoveries, awards and regulatory decisions are predictive evidence; they do not resolve this question.

I apply the client’s discovery-based matching rule. The laureates need not match the names in an option. A divided prize counts according to the larger-share/first-mentioned rule. This makes the official motivation—not the recipient roster—the relevant outcome.

## Evidence
The historical backbone is the complete set of annual Medicine prizes from 2000 through 2025. Under an inclusive matching rule, 17 of those 26 prize-years had earlier Lasker Basic or Clinical recognition of at least one Nobel-recognized component: 65.4%. This is a derived crosswalk between the official records, not a published selection probability, and partial matches in divided prizes count ([Nobel archive](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/all/); [Lasker archive](https://laskerfoundation.org/all-awards-winners/)).

Timing is much less predictable. There were 25 Lasker cycles in that window because the pandemic canceled the awards in 2020 ([cancellation notice](https://laskerfoundation.org/the-2020-lasker-awards/)). Only one cycle contained a defensible same-year Medicine overlap, an observed rate of 4%: the 2013 Lasker for regulated neurotransmitter release overlapped the Nobel for vesicle-traffic machinery. This was a nested scientific match, not an identical citation or recipient group ([2013 Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/2013-winners/); [Nobel record](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/all/)). The sample is small. It argues against treating a September award as an October preview; it does not cap any candidate’s probability at that historical rate.

**GLP-1 has the strongest combined case among the listed discoveries.** Its scientific foundation and therapeutic consequences both have repeated recognition. The 2024 Lasker Clinical award honored Habener, Mojsov and Knudsen; the 2025 Breakthrough award recognized five contributors across the discovery-to-treatment chain ([Lasker citation](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/glp-1-based-therapy-for-obesity/); [Breakthrough announcement](https://breakthroughprize.org/News/91)). Clarivate’s September 17, 2026 announcement added recognition for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, while explicitly disclaiming prediction of a particular year’s Nobel recipients ([Clarivate announcement](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/)).

The medical benefit extends beyond glucose control and weight loss. The FDA approved semaglutide’s cardiovascular-risk indication on March 8, 2024 ([FDA decision](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-treatment-reduce-risk-serious-heart-problems-specifically-adults-obesity-or)). I read this as established clinical validation, not merely public enthusiasm. Different award rosters reveal an attribution problem because the Nobel permits at most three recipients, but that warrants a modest discount—not exclusion of the discovery ([Nobel rules](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/facts-on-the-nobel-prize-in-physiology-or-medicine/)). The overlapping recognition signals are not independent evidence.

Orexin receives the largest current-year upgrade. The September 9, 2026 Lasker announcement recognized Mignot and Yanagisawa for identifying orexin and connecting its deficiency to narcolepsy ([dated announcement](https://laskerfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2026-press-release2.pdf)). The FDA approved oveporexton, marketed as Orzeyful, on August 5, 2026. It activates the orexin receptor system implicated by the discovery. The approval release reports two randomized, placebo-controlled studies totaling 273 adults, each lasting 12 weeks; calendar enrollment dates are not supplied there ([FDA approval](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-drug-treat-full-range-narcolepsy-type-1-symptoms)). This creates a coherent physiology-to-disease-to-treatment story. I raise orexin into the leading tier, but discount the fresh-award timing signal and the short clinical record.

The remaining listed discoveries retain meaningful probability. These are my judgments about annual selection, not rankings of scientific merit:

| Discovery | Forecast | Main consideration |
|---|---:|---|
| Optogenetics | 7% | The [2021 Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/light-sensitive-microbial-proteins-optogenetics/) validates a field-changing experimental method. I do not require broad clinical use for Medicine eligibility. |
| Unfolded protein response | 6% | The [2014 Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/unfolded-protein-response/) supports a bounded, fundamental cellular mechanism. Clear attribution helps; recent headline absence carries little negative weight. |
| CAR-T therapy | 6% | The [2024 Gairdner](https://www.gairdner.org/resource-hub/2024-canada-gairdner-award-winners-announced) and [2026 Tang Prize](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097) reinforce clinical readiness. Broad cell-therapy framing creates a resolution risk. |
| Chaperone-mediated folding | 5% | The [2011 Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/chaperone-assisted-protein-folding/) establishes the fundamental discovery. Hartl’s [September 18, 2026 Keio recognition](https://www.keio.ac.jp/en/press-release/20260918-press-01/) supplies a fresh, modest corroborating signal. |
| PCSK9 | 4% | The FDA’s [July 2026 oral-inhibitor announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-oral-pcsk9-inhibitor-lower-ldl-cholesterol-adults-high-cholesterol) strengthens translation. I give a new delivery modality less weight than validation of a previously untreatable mechanism. |
| Wnt signaling/organoids | 3% | [Gairdner’s account](https://www.gairdner.org/winner/roel-nusse) connects Wnt biology with stem cells and organoids. The combined option leaves uncertainty over the eventual motivation’s scope. |
| Leptin | 3% | The [2010 Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/leptin-a-hormone-that-regulates-appetite-and-body-weight/) supports a foundational physiological discovery. I rank GLP-1 above it on established therapeutic consequences. |
| Breast/ovarian susceptibility genes | 2% | [King’s Lasker account](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/breast-cancer-genetics-and-human-rights/) documents major preventive impact and the distinct mapping and gene-identification contributions. Attribution is less compact. |
| Anti-TNF therapy | 2% | The [2003 Lasker](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/anti-tnf-for-treating-rheumatoid-arthritis/) establishes a mature, transformative clinical case. I impose neither an automatic overdue premium nor a penalty simply for waiting. |
| Next-generation sequencing | 2% | The [2024 Gairdner](https://www.gairdner.org/resource-hub/2024-canada-gairdner-award-winners-announced) validates its importance. The [1980 Chemistry sequencing prize](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/1980/press-release/1000/) supplies a direct category-routing precedent. |

Other contains strong competitors, not just unforeseen outsiders. Optical coherence tomography has the 2023 Clinical Lasker and current Clarivate recognition ([OCT citation](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/optical-coherence-tomography/); [2026 Clarivate list](https://clarivate.com/news/clarivate-reveals-citation-laureates-2026-recognizing-transformative-scientific-breakthroughs/)). Further omitted discoveries include cGAS DNA sensing, integrins, low-complexity protein domains and cystic-fibrosis therapy ([cGAS](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/cgas-enzyme-that-senses-self-and-foreign-dna/); [integrins](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/integrins-mediators-of-cell-matrix-cell-adhesion/); [2025 research awards](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/2025-winners/)). The current Lasker cycle also recognized an unlisted bispecific-antibody treatment for hemophilia A ([2026 announcement](https://laskerfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/2026-press-release2.pdf)). These candidates justify substantial probability outside the supplied slate. The 32.0% allocation is my coverage judgment, not an observed base rate.

For the calculation, I began with an equal-weight linear pool of the supplied assessments. I treated their shared evidence as correlated, not as separate confirmations. I then applied judgmental relative-weight multipliers: 1.10 for GLP-1, UPR and chaperones; 1.05 for optogenetics; 1.03 for PCSK9; 1.15 for anti-TNF; 0.90 for orexin and CAR-T; 0.95 for sequencing; and 1.00 for the remaining named discoveries. These adjustments reduce fresh-award and roster signals, preserve fundamental-science cases, and remove unsupported waiting-time penalties.

I fixed Other at 32.0% and normalized the named weights to the remaining 68.0%. Formally, \(P_i=0.68b_im_i/\sum_j b_jm_j\), where \(b_i\) is the pooled starting probability and \(m_i\) is the review multiplier. This is an elicited forecast, not a fitted Nobel model. No prediction-market prices enter the estimate. The JSON decimals preserve the calculation; they do not imply comparable empirical precision.

## What's non-obvious
**An exact recipient-roster match can still point to the wrong resolution option.** The 2026 Tang citation names Rosenberg, Sadelain and June, but honors both tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy and CAR-T, naming the former first ([official citation](https://www.tang-prize.org/en/media_detail.php?id=2097)). A Nobel with that discovery ordering and equal shares would resolve to Other under the client’s rules. Conversely, a GLP-1 prize with a different trio would still match GLP-1. Discovery boundaries deserve more attention than guessing names.

The historical recognition statistic also runs in the wrong direction for a common forecasting shortcut. Frequent prior Lasker recognition among Nobel winners does not mean a newly selected Lasker discovery has a high immediate Nobel probability. Nor does a long wait establish declining prospects: the Medicine awards for hepatitis C and microRNA followed much earlier Lasker recognition ([HCV award history](https://laskerfoundation.org/2020-nobel-prize-in-medicine/); [microRNA recognition](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/2008-winners/); [Nobel archive](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-laureates-in-physiology-or-medicine/all/)). I therefore reject strong fresh-award, overdue and field-rotation rules.

## Uncertainties
The largest gap is the confidential institutional choice. Nominations and evaluations remain secret for 50 years, so public recognition cannot establish the current shortlist ([confidentiality rules](https://www.nobelprize.org/nomination)). I did not verify a public leak identifying the winner. A validated discovery-level record of unsuccessful candidates would improve annual-hazard estimates; winner histories alone cannot supply that denominator.

I did not turn the supplied bibliometrics into likelihood ratios. They stop before the forecast year, mix career-stage comparisons and lack a nonwinner control group. There are also date-quality flags: the supplied Hartl publication window begins before the birth year reported by his institution ([institutional biography](https://www.biochem.mpg.de/6859461/PM_20190905_Hartl_Breakthrough_EN.pdf)). Without underlying author records, I cannot distinguish metadata errors from attribution errors.

The remaining uncertainty concerns slate coverage, Medicine-versus-Chemistry routing and the motivation’s wording. As a sensitivity check, moving Other between 25% and 45% while preserving the named discoveries’ relative weights moves GLP-1 between 19% and 14%. That is a model-sensitivity range, not a statistical confidence interval. The durable conclusion is a dispersed forecast: GLP-1 leads the named choices, orexin has strong current-year validation, and omitted discoveries retain the largest combined share.
sub_write_ups:
## Forecast basis

I treated **October 1, 2026 at 22:34 UTC** as the information cutoff. The prize is scheduled for announcement on **October 5, 2026 at 11:30 CEST at the earliest**. The Nobel Committee presents its recommendation in September, but the full Nobel Assembly makes the final selection by vote in October, normally immediately before the announcement. Consequently, recent public prizes are useful evidence of scientific recognition, but they are not evidence that the Nobel decision has already leaked. 

I first made an estimate using only non-market evidence. I then searched Metaculus, Manifold, Kalshi, and Polymarket for a directly relevant market. I found no applicable liquid market or public forecasting aggregate, so there was no market-based adjustment.

## Method

I used a semi-quantitative ensemble with five considerations:

1. **Scientific importance and maturity:** whether the discovery has transformed physiology, medicine, or biomedical research and has had roughly 20–40 years to mature.
2. **Precursor recognition:** Lasker, Breakthrough, Gairdner, Tang, Keio, Clarivate Citation Laureate, and comparable awards. I discounted these because award juries share reputational networks and are not statistically independent.
3. **Attribution fit:** the Nobel can recognize at most three living people. Discoveries with a clean one-to-three-person history receive a substantial advantage over fields with five or more defensible pioneers.
4. **Category fit:** discoveries that are naturally framed as physiology or medicine are favored over research technologies that could instead receive Chemistry recognition.
5. **Current weak signals:** unusually recent therapeutic validation, concentrated 2026 award activity, institutional profiles, event calendars, and official-site anomalies. No credible Nobel-origin leak, staged Nobel page, candidate travel anomaly, or cancellation was found.

I assigned **34.45% to Other** before distributing the remaining probability. This is a judgmental outside-option prior, not a frequency calculated from a random sample. It is intentionally large because credible omitted candidates include optical coherence tomography, immune-cell adhesion receptors, cGAS–STING signaling, B- and T-cell discovery, phase separation, and gene-editing technologies. Clarivate's 2026 Medicine selections themselves included two unlisted discoveries—optical coherence tomography and immune adhesion receptors—alongside GLP-1. 

The user-provided bibliometrics were used as a secondary cross-check. They confirm that most listed discoveries are genuinely Nobel-caliber, but citation volume and patent reach are weak at distinguishing which one the committee will choose in a particular year. Attribution, category boundaries, clinical maturation, and the committee's desire to recognize a specific discovery matter at least as much.

## Leading candidates

### 1. Orexin and sleep/wake regulation — 14.15%

This is my leading listed option. Emmanuel Mignot and Masashi Yanagisawa received the **2026 Lasker Basic Medical Research Award** for identifying orexin's role in maintaining wakefulness and establishing that orexin deficiency causes narcolepsy. The discovery dates to roughly 1998–2000 and therefore has a Nobel-typical maturation period. 

The unusually important weak signal is the **August 5, 2026 FDA approval of Orzeyful/oveporexton**, the first approved treatment that directly restores orexin signaling and targets the underlying biology of narcolepsy type 1. This turns an elegant neurophysiological discovery into a completed discovery-to-therapy narrative immediately before Nobel season. ([takeda.com](https://www.takeda.com/newsroom/newsreleases/2026/orzeyful-approved-narcolepsy/?utm_source=openai))

Its primary advantage is attribution: a Nobel motivation centered on orexin deficiency, narcolepsy, and sleep regulation could cleanly recognize Mignot and Yanagisawa. Its disadvantage is that Luis de Lecea and others have legitimate claims to the independent discovery of hypocretin/orexin. I therefore treat the Lasker and FDA developments as strong but not remotely decisive; a 50%-type estimate would underweight Nobel unpredictability and the many omitted discoveries.

### 2. GLP-1 biology and therapies — 11.45%

GLP-1 has perhaps the largest present-day public-health impact. The 2024 Lasker award recognized Joel Habener, Svetlana Mojsov, and Lotte Bjerre Knudsen; the 2025 Breakthrough Prize recognized five contributors, including Daniel Drucker and Jens Juul Holst; and Clarivate's September 2026 Citation Laureates selected Drucker, Holst, and Mojsov. ([ms-fund.keio.ac.jp](https://www.ms-fund.keio.ac.jp/en/prize/the-2026-keio-medical-science-prize-awardees.html?utm_source=openai))

The central negative is the **three-person attribution problem**. Major award bodies have selected materially different combinations of Habener, Mojsov, Holst, Drucker, and Knudsen. Because the question resolves by discovery rather than exact laureates, this does not create a resolution problem, but it may cause the Nobel Assembly to postpone GLP-1 rather than make a controversial exclusion. The 2026 Clarivate selection is a recognition signal, not inside information; Clarivate notes that its selections can precede an eventual Nobel by many years. 

### 3. CAR-T therapy — 7.15%

CAR-T received a conspicuous cluster of recent recognition. The **2026 Tang Prize** selected Carl June, Michel Sadelain, and Steven Rosenberg—the exact trio in the option—under an explicit three-awardee framework for cellular cancer immunotherapy. Sadelain also received major recent recognition for the conception and implementation of CD19 CAR-T therapy. 

This is a meaningful weak signal because another prestigious committee has demonstrated that the discovery can be compressed into a Nobel-compatible three-person package. Nevertheless, foundational credit also extends to Zelig Eshhar, Bruce Levine, Isabelle Rivière, and others. I additionally apply a modest thematic penalty because the **2025 Medicine Nobel concerned peripheral immune tolerance**, following the 2018 cancer-immunotherapy award. Back-to-back immunology prizes are possible, but somewhat less likely than a change of field.

## Middle tier

### Optogenetics — 5.55%

Optogenetics transformed experimental neuroscience and has an excellent impact profile. The problem is attribution: different awards have selected different combinations of Deisseroth, Hegemann, Miesenböck, Boyden, Oesterhelt, and Nagel. A major BBVA award, for example, recognized Boyden, Deisseroth, and Miesenböck, whereas the 2021 Lasker formulation emphasized Oesterhelt, Hegemann, and Deisseroth. It also remains primarily a research method rather than a broadly established therapy. 

### Chaperone-mediated protein folding — 5.55%

Horwich and Hartl form a clean two-person discovery package. Their 2011 Lasker citation described how ATP-dependent chaperone machinery overturns the assumption that cellular proteins fold unaided. A fresh signal arrived on **September 18, 2026**, when Hartl received the 2026 Keio Medical Science Prize for molecular-chaperone-mediated protein folding. ([keio.ac.jp](https://www.keio.ac.jp/en/press-release/20260918-press-01/?utm_source=openai))

The main negatives are category ambiguity—this could be considered biochemistry or Chemistry—and overlap with other proteostasis discoveries such as the unfolded protein response and autophagy.

### Unfolded protein response — 5.45%

Mori and Walter have one of the cleanest attribution structures in the field. The 2014 Lasker Award recognized them specifically for discovering the unfolded protein response, an essential cellular quality-control pathway, and Walter subsequently received a Breakthrough Prize for the same work. 

It lacks the fresh clinical catalyst of orexin and the 2026 recognition burst of CAR-T, GLP-1, or chaperones. It also sits near previously rewarded cellular quality-control mechanisms, especially autophagy.

### PCSK9 and LDL-cholesterol regulation — 4.45%

PCSK9 offers a strong genetics-to-drug-development narrative: Nabil Seidah identified PCSK9, while Helen Hobbs and Jonathan Cohen showed that loss-of-function variants produce low LDL cholesterol and protection from coronary heart disease, helping inspire PCSK9 inhibitors. 

A minor weak signal is that Hobbs was announced as the **2026 Abarca Prize winner on October 1**, the forecast date, for protective human-genetic discoveries leading to cardiovascular and liver therapies. I give this only a small update because it is an independent award, not a Nobel leak, and PCSK9 attribution spans protein discovery, disease mutations, protective variants, and pharmaceutical development. 

## Lower tier

### Wnt signaling and organoids — 2.75%

Clevers and Nusse are exceptionally influential: Clevers received a Breakthrough Prize for Wnt signaling in stem cells and cancer, while Nusse received major recognition for pioneering the Wnt pathway. 

The option combines at least two related but separable accomplishments—Wnt-pathway biology and adult-stem-cell organoid culture. Foundational credit also includes Harold Varmus, Toshiro Sato, and numerous developmental and stem-cell biologists, making a clean Nobel motivation less straightforward.

### Inherited breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility genes — 2.65%

Mary-Claire King's mapping of the BRCA1 locus and the later identification of BRCA1 and BRCA2 transformed cancer-risk prediction and preventive medicine. The Lasker Foundation's account, however, distinguishes King's linkage discovery, the later Myriad cloning work, and Michael Stratton's BRCA2 contribution. 

This is medically important and mature, but the credit chain is divided across different discoveries and teams. That lowers the probability of this exact combined motivation.

### Leptin and hormonal regulation of body weight — 2.45%

Friedman's discovery of leptin fundamentally established adipose tissue as an endocrine organ regulating appetite and body weight. He has received Gairdner and Breakthrough recognition. 

The canonical discovery history also includes Douglas Coleman's earlier parabiosis work, while O'Rahilly's major contribution concerns human obesity genetics and leptin-deficiency physiology. With Coleman deceased, a Friedman–O'Rahilly Nobel would require a somewhat different framing from the standard historical account. GLP-1's stronger present therapeutic impact also competes for the same broad metabolic theme.

### TNF as a therapeutic target — 2.45%

Feldmann and Maini have a very clean, clinically transformative case and shared the 2003 Lasker Clinical Award for anti-TNF therapy in rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune diseases. 

Its low probability is not a judgment that it is undeserving. Rather, it has been a top candidate for more than two decades without being chosen, and the 2025 Nobel's immune-tolerance theme creates a substantial short-term recency penalty.

### Next-generation DNA sequencing — 1.50%

Next-generation sequencing is one of the most transformative technologies listed. The 2026 Princess of Asturias Award selected Klenerman, Balasubramanian, and Pascal Mayer for developing today's most widely used sequencing technologies. 

I place it low specifically for the Medicine prize because sequencing technology is more naturally a Chemistry candidate. The omission of Mayer from the option's people does not affect resolution by discovery, but it illustrates the attribution issue.

## Other — 34.45%

Other remains the single most likely outcome because the named options are only a curated subset of Nobel-caliber medicine. The strongest concrete omitted candidate is **optical coherence tomography**, with a clean three-person group—James Fujimoto, David Huang, and Eric Swanson—and major clinical impact. Clarivate also highlighted Timothy Springer's immune-cell adhesion-receptor work in its 2026 Medicine cohort. Other plausible omissions include cGAS–STING signaling, B- and T-cell differentiation, phase-separated cellular condensates, angiogenesis, and precision gene editing. 

## Calibration and principal uncertainty

The forecast's central judgment is that the **August FDA approval plus the September Lasker award make orexin the strongest named option**, but not overwhelmingly so. Recent external awards are correlated indicators of scientific maturity, not observations of the secret Nobel deliberations. The largest source of uncertainty is therefore not whether these listed discoveries are worthy; it is whether the Assembly chooses one of them in 2026 rather than one of the many omitted discoveries.

## 2. Historical calibration: a fresh Lasker is not a same-year Nobel forecast

The most important base-rate check was whether a September Lasker award commonly identifies that October's Nobel Medicine discovery. The historical exercise compared **2000–2025 inclusive: 26 Nobel years and 25 years with Lasker awards**, since Lasker canceled its 2020 awards during the pandemic. The unit is an annual discovery award, not an individual recipient. Matches were made by substantive discovery overlap, with recipient overlap as a cross-check. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/all-awards-winners/))

The result was:

| Same-year relationship, 2000–2025 | Matches / Lasker-award years | Observed rate | Calculated 95% Wilson interval |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Basic Lasker → Nobel Medicine | 1 / 25 | 4.0% | 0.71%–19.54% |
| Clinical Lasker → Nobel Medicine | 0 / 25 | 0.0% | 0%–13.32% |
| Either category → Nobel Medicine | 1 / 25 | 4.0% | 0.71%–19.54% |

The sole same-year overlap was **2013**: the Basic Lasker recognized Scheller and Südhof's regulated neurotransmitter-release work, while the Nobel recognized Rothman, Schekman, and Südhof's vesicle-traffic machinery. This is an overlapping discovery, not an identical recipient slate. The comparison can be reproduced from the Foundation's annual winner pages and official Nobel motivations; all other award-years in the specified window had no same-year Basic or Clinical discovery match. ([laskerfoundation.org](https://laskerfoundation.org/winners/2013-winners/))

I recalculated the intervals in Python. With a Jeffreys Beta(0.5, 0.5) prior, the Basic/either rate has a posterior median of approximately **4.67%**, with a 95% credible interval of **0.44%–17.21%**. These are uncertainty intervals for the historical same-year rate—not intervals for orexin's 2026 probability. The sample is small, matching requires judgment, and scientific-prize selection is not a stationary random process.

This evidence prevents two mistakes: treating the 2026 Lasker as a near-certain preview, and confusing the eventual fraction of Lasker recipients who receive some Nobel with the probability of a Medicine Nobel immediately that year. It does **not** cap orexin at 4%; orexin also has independent evidence of maturity and clinical validation. Nor does the zero Clinical count imply that a clinical discovery cannot win.

Approval is a strong mechanistic-validation signal, but this is a smaller and shorter clinical evidence base than GLP-1's established outcomes record.
